questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:
1. It cannot vote on the Demand for Grants.
2. It can pass a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
3. A Money Bill must be returned by it within 14 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.history: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House with limited financial powers; the Constitution reserves confidence and money matters for the directly elected House.
questions.discussion: Demands for Grants are voted only in the Lok Sabha, so statement 1 is correct. The no-confidence motion lies exclusively with the Lok Sabha, so statement 2 is wrong. A Money Bill goes to the Rajya Sabha only for recommendation and must be returned within 14 days, making statement 3 correct.

wh.what: Asymmetry between the two Houses on money and confidence
wh.why: The Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha alone
wh.how: Articles 109, 113 and 75(3)

questions.status: The Rajya Sabha retains equal powers on constitutional amendments and on removing the President, which is why it is not a wholly weak House.
why_wrong: Statement 2 is wrong: the no-confidence motion is a Lok Sabha device only.
Statement 2 is wrong, so any option containing it fails.
Statement 2 is wrong, so the all-correct option fails.
questions.tip: On any question mixing both Houses, check the three money items first: Money Bill, Demands for Grants, no-confidence motion. All three belong to the Lok Sabha.
questions.improve: Write a two-column table of exclusive Lok Sabha powers and equal powers of both Houses.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A machine costs ₹1,00,000 with a residual value of ₹10,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Annual depreciation under the straight line method is:
questions.history: Straight line depreciation spreads the depreciable amount, cost minus residual value, equally over the useful life.
questions.discussion: The depreciable amount is 90,000, and dividing by 5 gives 18,000 a year. Ignoring the residual value is the standard trap, and it produces the 20,000 distractor.

wh.how: (Cost - Residual value) / Useful life
wh.why: Matching of cost with the revenue it helps earn

questions.status: The Companies Act 2013, Schedule II, prescribes useful lives for WDV and SLM, and Ind AS 16 governs measurement.
why_wrong: ₹20,000 ignores the residual value of ₹10,000.
₹22,000 would arise if residual value were added rather than subtracted.
₹16,000 corresponds to a residual value of ₹20,000.
questions.tip: Always subtract salvage first. If the question gives a residual value, it is there to be used.
questions.improve: Compute WDV depreciation for the same figures and compare the two first-year charges.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Accountancy; Companies Act 2013 Schedule II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical formula of common salt is:
questions.history: Common salt is sodium chloride, formed by the ionic bond between a sodium cation and a chloride anion in a face-centred cubic lattice.
questions.discussion: The other options are also familiar salts, which is exactly the trap: potassium chloride is a salt substitute, sodium bicarbonate is baking soda, and calcium carbonate is limestone.

wh.where: Seawater, rock salt and salt pans
wh.why: Essential for electrolyte balance and food preservation

questions.status: Iodised salt is the main vehicle for iodine supplementation in India's public health programmes.
why_wrong: KCl is potassium chloride, used as a low-sodium salt substitute.
NaHCO₃ is baking soda, sodium bicarbonate.
CaCO₃ is calcium carbonate, found in chalk and limestone.
questions.tip: Learn the everyday names table: NaCl salt, NaHCO₃ baking soda, CaO quicklime, Ca(OH)₂ slaked lime, CaSO₄ plaster of Paris.
questions.improve: Write ten common names with formulas in one table.
questions.source: NCERT Class X Science, Acids Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Ramsar Convention deals with the conservation of:
questions.history: Signed at Ramsar in Iran in 1971, the convention is the oldest global environmental treaty, focused on wise use of wetlands; India joined in 1982.
questions.discussion: Ramsar sites in India now number over 80, including Chilika, Keoladeo and Sundarbans, and designation brings monitoring obligations rather than new policing powers.

wh.why: Wetlands were being lost faster than forests

questions.status: India has expanded its Ramsar list sharply since 2019 as part of wetland conservation targets.
why_wrong: Migratory birds are covered by the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS).
Desertification is the UNCCD, signed in 1994.
Ozone substances fall under the Montreal Protocol.
questions.tip: One convention per problem: Ramsar wetlands, CMS birds, UNCCD desertification, Montreal ozone, Basel hazardous waste, CITES trade.
questions.improve: Build a six-row table of environmental conventions with year, place and subject.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
questions.history: The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and runs about 1,465 km to the Bay of Bengal, earning the name Dakshin Ganga.
questions.discussion: It drains Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, and its delta is a major rice and aquaculture belt.

wh.where: Source in Nashik district, mouth in Andhra Pradesh
wh.why: Large basin area across the Deccan plateau
wh.how: Fed by monsoon rainfall and tributaries such as the Indravati

questions.status: Inter-State water sharing among riparian States remains a live dispute, and Polavaram project is contested.
why_wrong: The Krishna is the second longest peninsular river at about 1,400 km.
The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea and is shorter.
The Kaveri is about 800 km and mainly a delta river.
questions.tip: Peninsular length order: Godavari, Krishna, Narmada, Mahanadi, Kaveri.
questions.improve: Learn source and mouth for the five major peninsular rivers in one line each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment

questions.subject: GST
questions.q: Input Tax Credit under GST allows a registered dealer to:
options: Claim a refund of all taxes paid by consumers
Set off tax paid on inputs against tax payable on output
Charge tax at a lower rate than notified
questions.history: ITC removes the cascading effect of tax on tax by allowing credit for tax already paid on purchases used in the course of business.
questions.discussion: Credit is available only for business use, with blocked credits listed for items such as personal consumption and certain motor vehicles, and the credit must appear in the supplier's filed return.

wh.how: Output tax liability minus eligible input credit
wh.why: Tax should fall on value added, not on every transaction

questions.status: The e-invoicing and GSTR-2B matching systems now govern credit eligibility in practice.
why_wrong: Refunds to consumers are a separate welfare question, not ITC.
Registration thresholds apply regardless of credit.
Rates are notified by the Council, not chosen by the dealer.
questions.tip: ITC is a set-off, not a refund. You subtract credit from liability, and only excess credit may become a refund.
questions.improve: Work through one purchase-sale cycle and compute net GST payable.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: GST was introduced in India through which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.history: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 created the GST Council under Article 279A and gave concurrent taxing powers to the Union and States, effective 1 July 2017.
questions.discussion: GST replaced a web of central and State indirect taxes with a destination-based value added tax, with CGST, SGST and IGST as its three forms.

wh.who: GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister
wh.why: To remove cascading taxes and create one national market

questions.status: A five-year compensation guarantee ended in 2022; rate rationalisation into a simpler slab structure is under discussion.
why_wrong: The 99th Amendment created the NJAC, later struck down.
The 100th Amendment implemented the India-Bangladesh land boundary agreement.
The 102nd Amendment gave constitutional status to the NCBC.
questions.tip: The 101st is GST — remember it as the tax chapter. The 102nd is the Backward Classes Commission.
questions.improve: Learn the GST Council's composition and voting formula, 75 per cent weighted voting with the Union holding one-third.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Preamble cannot be enforced in a court of law.
Reason (R): The Preamble is a part of the Constitution and can be amended.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.history: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, subject to the basic structure doctrine.
questions.discussion: Both statements are true but they answer different questions. The Preamble is unenforceable because it confers no rights and imposes no duties; it is amendable because it is part of the Constitution. Amendability is not the reason for unenforceability.

wh.why: Two true propositions can be causally unrelated
wh.how: Test whether R independently explains A

questions.status: The Preamble has been amended once, by the 42nd Amendment, which added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'.
why_wrong: R does not explain why the Preamble is unenforceable.
R is true: the Preamble was amended in 1976.
A is true: courts have repeatedly held the Preamble non-enforceable.
questions.tip: In assertion-reason, first check truth of each statement separately, then check causation. Most errors come from skipping the causation step.
questions.improve: Practise ten assertion-reason items, writing one line on why R does or does not explain A.
questions.source: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.history: Occurrence keeps both the double c and the double r, following the pattern of occur plus the suffix ence.
questions.discussion: When a word ending in a single consonant is stressed on the last syllable and takes a suffix, the consonant doubles; occur follows that rule.

wh.how: Check doubling after a stressed final syllable
wh.why: Spelling carries direct marks

questions.status: Exams repeat a small set of commonly misspelt words, so a list of 100 covers most cases.
why_wrong: Occurence drops the second r.
Ocurrence drops the second c.
Occurrance uses a instead of e in the suffix.
questions.tip: Learn the doubling rule once and it covers occurred, occurrence, beginning and committed together.
questions.improve: Write the twenty most commonly misspelt exam words five times each.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.history: Mitochondria generate most cellular ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, which is why they earned the powerhouse label.
questions.discussion: They have their own circular DNA and ribosomes and divide independently, evidence for the endosymbiotic theory that they were once free-living bacteria.

wh.how: Electron transport chain builds a proton gradient to make ATP
wh.why: ATP is the energy currency every cell process draws on

questions.status: Mitochondrial DNA is inherited maternally, which is the basis of mitochondrial lineage studies.
why_wrong: Ribosomes synthesise proteins.
The Golgi body packages and modifies proteins.
Lysosomes digest waste using hydrolytic enzymes.
questions.tip: One organelle, one job: ribosome makes, Golgi packs, lysosome digests, mitochondria pays the bills.
questions.improve: Draw a cell and label ten organelles with one function each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Biology, Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a certain code, MOUSE is written as NPVTF. How is CAT written in that code?
questions.history: Each letter of the word is shifted one place forward in the alphabet, a simple substitution code.
questions.discussion: M to N, O to P, U to V confirms the +1 shift, so C becomes D, A becomes B and T becomes U.

wh.how: Compare letter positions between word and code
wh.why: A standard coding question type

questions.status: Tougher variants use alternating shifts or reverse alphabet positions (A=26).
why_wrong: DAT leaves A unchanged, which breaks the uniform shift.
BZS shifts backwards, the opposite direction.
DCU shifts the first two letters but not the third.
questions.tip: Write the alphabet with positions 1 to 26 and the shift becomes arithmetic, not memory.
questions.improve: Practise reverse alphabet coding and mixed-shift codes next.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which index is used as the headline measure of retail inflation in India?
questions.history: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended CPI-Combined as the nominal anchor, and the RBI Act was amended in 2016 to target CPI inflation at 4 per cent with a 2 per cent band.
questions.discussion: WPI tracks wholesale prices without services, so it lags and misses the household basket; CPI includes services and is the policy target.

wh.why: It reflects the household consumption basket
wh.how: Weighted price index across rural and urban centres

questions.status: The monetary policy target is 4 per cent CPI inflation with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 per cent, reviewed every five years.
why_wrong: WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser and excludes services.
IIP measures industrial output growth, not prices.
The GDP deflator is the broadest price measure but not used as the policy target.
questions.tip: CPI is the policy anchor, WPI is a supplementary indicator, and the deflator is for national accounts.
questions.improve: Compare CPI and WPI weights for food, fuel and services in a small table.
questions.source: RBI Act amendment 2016; MoSPI CPI releases

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30?
questions.history: The minute hand moves 6° per minute and the hour hand 0.5° per minute, so at 3:30 the hour hand has already moved 15° past 3.
questions.discussion: Using the formula |30H - 5.5M| gives |90 - 165| = 75°, matching the intuitive picture of the hour hand no longer sitting exactly on 3.

wh.why: A standard reasoning question

questions.status: Variants ask for the time when hands coincide or are opposite.
why_wrong: 80° does not match the formula for any standard half-hour position.
85° comes from treating the hour hand as stationary at 3.
90° is the angle at exactly 3:00, not 3:30.
questions.tip: Remember 5.5 as the relative speed of the hands in degrees per minute. The formula then writes itself.
questions.improve: Find the times between 3 and 4 when the hands are together and opposite.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.history: Compound interest adds each year's interest to the principal, so the second year earns interest on the first year's interest as well.
questions.discussion: The standard shortcut is net effective rate for two years: 10 + 10 + 10×10/100 = 21 per cent, giving 2,100 directly.

wh.why: Banks use compounding for term deposits and loans

questions.status: Exams increasingly test half-yearly and quarterly compounding, where the rate is divided and time multiplied.
why_wrong: ₹2,000 is the simple interest for the same period.
₹2,200 comes from applying 22 per cent, an error in the second-year interest base.
₹2,310 is the answer for 3 years at 10 per cent.
questions.tip: Two-year CI shortcut: net rate = 2r + r²/100. For 10 per cent it is 21 per cent, no long multiplication needed.
questions.improve: Learn the net-rate formula for three years as well: 3r + 3r²/100 + r³/10000.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.q: The concept of the primary group was introduced by:
questions.history: Cooley introduced the primary group in 1909 to describe small, face-to-face, emotionally close groups such as family and neighbourhood.
questions.discussion: Primary groups build the self through what Cooley called the looking-glass self, while secondary groups are impersonal and goal oriented, such as a workplace.

wh.why: To distinguish intimate groups from formal ones

questions.status: Digital communication has blurred the distinction, with online communities showing both intimacy and scale.
why_wrong: Durkheim is associated with social facts, anomie and suicide typology.
Weber is known for ideal types and the Protestant ethic thesis.
Parsons developed structural functionalism and pattern variables.
questions.tip: Cooley for primary group and looking-glass self. Both belong to the same thinker, so learn them as a pair.
questions.improve: Compare primary and secondary groups on five characteristics.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Sociology, Understanding Society

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Renaissance began in which country?
questions.history: The Renaissance began in the Italian city-states, especially Florence, in the fourteenth century, funded by mercantile wealth and sustained by classical manuscripts.
questions.discussion: Patronage by families such as the Medici, the fall of Constantinople pushing Greek scholars westward, and printing with movable type together created the conditions for its spread.

wh.why: Urban wealth, patronage and recovery of classical texts

questions.status: Historians now treat the Renaissance as one phase in a longer continuity rather than a sharp break with the medieval world.
why_wrong: France was important later, in the Enlightenment.
England produced the Elizabethan flowering but not the origin.
Germany was central to the Reformation, not the Renaissance.
questions.tip: Sequence them: Renaissance in Italy, Reformation in Germany, Enlightenment in France, Industrial Revolution in Britain.
questions.improve: List five Renaissance figures with their fields.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Themes in World History

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Right to Education was made a Fundamental Right by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.history: Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, after the Supreme Court in Unni Krishnan (1993) read education into Article 21.
questions.discussion: The amendment added Article 21A for children aged 6-14 and simultaneously changed Article 45 into a directive for early childhood care, showing how a court judgment can mature into constitutional text.

wh.what: Free and compulsory education as a fundamental right
wh.who: Parliament, following Unni Krishnan and Mohini Jain judgments
wh.why: Literacy was a constitutional promise stuck in the Directive Principles

questions.status: Implemented through the Right to Education Act, 2009; NEP 2020 now extends the policy focus to ages 3-18.
why_wrong: The 42nd Amendment is remembered for the mini-Constitution changes and Fundamental Duties, not Article 21A.
The 44th Amendment reversed several Emergency-era distortions of civil liberty.
The 93rd Amendment created reservation for OBCs in private educational institutions.
questions.tip: Anchor amendments to their theme: 42nd = duties and mini-constitution, 44th = undoing Emergency, 52nd = anti-defection, 86th = education, 101st = GST.
questions.improve: Build a one-page timeline of amendments 42 to 106 with the article each one touched.
questions.source: Constitution of India, Article 21A; 86th Amendment Act 2002

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?
questions.history: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, spanning Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was designated in 1986 as India's first under the UNESCO Man and Biosphere programme.
questions.discussion: Biosphere reserves have three zones: core, buffer and transition, and they are not the same as national parks or tiger reserves in legal status.

wh.why: To combine conservation with sustainable use and research

questions.status: India has 18 biosphere reserves, of which 12 are in the UNESCO world network.
why_wrong: Nanda Devi was designated in 1988, the second.
Sundarbans came in 1989.
Gulf of Mannar came in 1989.
questions.tip: Firsts in conservation: first biosphere reserve Nilgiri 1986, first national park Hailey (Jim Corbett) 1936, first tiger reserve Corbett 1973.
questions.improve: List India's biosphere reserves with State and UNESCO status.

questions.subject: Statistics
questions.q: Standard deviation is the:
options: Positive square root of the variance
Average of the deviations from the mean
Difference between the highest and lowest value
questions.history: Standard deviation is defined as the positive square root of the variance, restoring the original units of the data.
questions.discussion: Variance squares the deviations, which inflates the unit, so the square root brings the measure back to the same scale as the observations, making comparison meaningful.

wh.how: Square root of the average squared deviation from the mean
wh.why: It is expressed in the same units as the data

questions.status: Used widely in quality control, finance and the coefficient of variation.
why_wrong: Variance is the square of standard deviation, not the reverse.
The average of absolute deviations is the mean absolute deviation.
That is the range.
questions.tip: Variance is in squared units, standard deviation is in original units. If the question mentions units, it is standard deviation.
questions.improve: Compute variance and standard deviation for a five-value dataset by hand.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Statistics, Measures of Dispersion

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which writ literally means 'you may have the body' and is used to produce a detained person before the court?
questions.history: Habeas Corpus is a Latin phrase meaning 'to have the body', an ancient common-law remedy against unlawful detention.
questions.discussion: Unlike the other writs, it can be sought against a private person too and is not limited to public authorities. Courts have used it in cases of preventive detention and illegal custody.

wh.who: Any person in custody or a relative on their behalf
wh.why: Personal liberty is the most basic of fundamental rights
wh.how: The detaining authority must justify the detention

questions.status: Remains the primary judicial safeguard in preventive detention cases under Articles 22 and 21.
why_wrong: Mandamus commands a public authority to perform a duty it has refused to perform.
Quo Warranto questions the authority of a person holding a public office.
Certiorari asks a lower court to transfer its record for review.
questions.tip: Memorise writs by their Latin sense: mandamus = we command, quo warranto = by what authority, certiorari = to be certified.
questions.improve: Take one landmark case per writ — for example Maneka Gandhi for personal liberty.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the photoelectric effect:
1. The stopping potential depends on the intensity of incident light.
2. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons depends on the frequency of incident light.
3. Above the threshold frequency, the photoelectric current depends on the intensity of light.
questions.history: Einstein's photoelectric equation, hf = φ + Kmax, makes maximum kinetic energy a function of frequency alone, while current tracks the number of photons arriving.
questions.discussion: Stopping potential is a direct measure of maximum kinetic energy, so it depends on frequency and not intensity — statement 1 is wrong. Intensity changes the number of photons, hence the number of electrons and the current.

wh.how: hf = φ + eV₀
wh.why: Light arrives as discrete quanta, not as continuous energy

questions.status: The effect is the working principle of photomultiplier tubes and of photovoltaic cells, though cells rely on the internal photoelectric effect in semiconductors.
why_wrong: Statement 1 is wrong: stopping potential is intensity-independent.
Statement 1 is wrong, so this option fails.
Statement 1 is wrong.
questions.tip: Two rules settle every photoelectric question: frequency controls energy, intensity controls number.
questions.improve: Sketch the graph of stopping potential against frequency and label its slope and intercept.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Physics, Dual Nature of Radiation

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.q: The traditional four Ps of the marketing mix are:
questions.history: The four Ps were popularised by E. Jerome McCarthy in the 1960s as a framework for the controllable elements of a marketing decision.
questions.discussion: Services marketing extends this to seven Ps by adding people, process and physical evidence, a distinction examiners like to test.

wh.why: It groups the levers a marketer controls
wh.how: Each P answers a distinct question: what, how much, where, how to communicate

questions.status: Digital marketing has added data and personalisation as informal fifth and sixth levers, though the four Ps remain the base.
why_wrong: Profit is an outcome, not a marketing lever.
These are the service marketing extensions, missing product and place.
Plan and profit are not part of the mix.
questions.tip: Four Ps for goods, seven Ps for services. Remember the three extra as people, process, physical evidence.
questions.improve: Take a local product and write its four Ps in one line each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Business Studies, Marketing Management

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'benevolent'.
questions.history: Benevolent means wishing well, from Latin bene plus velle; malevolent is its exact opposite.
questions.discussion: The bene and male prefixes are the key: they recur in benefit, benediction, malice and malign, making the answer derivable without memorising the word.

wh.how: Use prefix roots to derive meaning
wh.why: Prefix knowledge answers unseen words

questions.status: Prefix-based vocabulary is tested heavily in banking mains.
why_wrong: Kind is a synonym.
Generous is a synonym.
Charitable is a synonym, not an antonym.
questions.tip: Learn the bene, mal, ben, mis and anti prefixes; they unlock dozens of exam words at once.
questions.improve: Write ten word pairs using bene and male prefixes.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Cost of goods sold is calculated as:
questions.history: Cost of goods sold equals the goods available for sale minus what remains unsold, which is opening stock plus purchases minus closing stock.
questions.discussion: With opening stock 20,000, purchases 80,000 and closing stock 30,000, COGS is 70,000. This figure then drives gross profit when deducted from net sales.

wh.how: Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock
wh.why: It separates trading results from operating expenses

questions.status: Under Ind AS, COGS presentation changes but the arithmetic identity stays the same.
why_wrong: Adding closing stock double counts goods still in hand.
Subtracting opening stock misstates goods available for sale.
This derives from the gross profit figure rather than computing it.
questions.tip: Think physically: what you started with, plus what you bought, minus what is left. The formula is just that sentence.
questions.improve: Prepare a trading account from a small trial balance to see COGS in use.

questions.subject: Management
questions.q: The principle of unity of command states that:
options: Each employee should receive orders from only one superior
One plan should guide the whole organisation
Authority should be concentrated at the top
Employees should be grouped by function
questions.history: Henri Fayol's unity of command principle holds that dual reporting creates confusion, conflict and diluted accountability.
questions.discussion: It is often confused with unity of direction, which concerns one head and one plan for activities with the same objective. Matrix structures deliberately violate unity of command to gain flexibility.

wh.why: Multiple bosses produce conflicting instructions

questions.status: Modern agile organisations accept dual reporting as a trade-off, while keeping accountability clear.
why_wrong: One plan and one head for similar activities is unity of direction.
Concentration of authority describes centralisation.
Grouping by function is departmentalisation.
questions.tip: Command is about people, direction is about activities. That one distinction answers most Fayol questions.
questions.improve: Learn all fourteen Fayol principles with a one-line example each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Business Studies, Principles of Management

questions.subject: OOP
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of object oriented programming?
questions.history: The four pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction; compilation is a build process, not a design principle.
questions.discussion: Encapsulation hides state behind methods, inheritance reuses behaviour, polymorphism lets one interface serve many types, and abstraction exposes only what matters.

wh.why: To model software around data and behaviour rather than procedures
wh.how: Classes, objects, interfaces and inheritance hierarchies

questions.status: Modern design favours composition over inheritance, but the four pillars remain the standard syllabus framing.
why_wrong: Encapsulation is a pillar.
Inheritance is a pillar.
Polymorphism is a pillar.
questions.tip: Four pillars: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction. Anything about tooling is not a pillar.
questions.improve: Write one Java or C++ example demonstrating each pillar.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced which body, and on what date was it constituted?
questions.history: A Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015 replaced the Planning Commission with NITI Aayog, ending the era of five-year plan allocations.
questions.discussion: The shift was from directive central planning to a think tank that advises States, with cooperative and competitive federalism as its stated model.

wh.who: Chaired by the Prime Minister, with a Vice-Chairman and CEO
wh.why: Planning Commission's one-size model had outlived its use

questions.status: Publishes the SDG India Index, MPI, and runs Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks programmes.
why_wrong: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280 and still exists.
The National Development Council still exists as a body of Chief Ministers.
The date and the replaced body are both wrong here.
questions.tip: Two dates to fix: Planning Commission 15 March 1950, NITI Aayog 1 January 2015.
questions.improve: Write the institutional structure of NITI Aayog and three of its indices.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Which Harappan site is known for its brick dockyard?
questions.history: Lothal in Gujarat, on the Bhogava river near the Gulf of Khambhat, has a trapezoidal basin identified as a dockyard with a sluice gate.
questions.discussion: The dockyard supports the reading that Harappans ran long-distance maritime trade with the Persian Gulf, corroborated by Mesopotamian seals found at the site.
questions.status: A national maritime heritage complex is being developed at Lothal, linking ancient trade to modern shipping history.
why_wrong: Kalibangan in Rajasthan is known for ploughed fields and fire altars.
Dholavira is known for its water management and three-part town plan.
Banawali in Haryana is known for its radial street pattern.
questions.tip: One identifier per site is enough: Lothal dockyard, Dholavira water, Kalibangan ploughed field, Rakhigarhi largest site.
questions.improve: Build a site-to-feature flashcard set of 20 Harappan sites.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part I; ASI Lothal

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Current assets are ₹4,00,000 and current liabilities ₹2,00,000. The current ratio is:
questions.history: The current ratio compares short-term assets with short-term obligations, and a ratio of 2:1 is conventionally treated as comfortable.
questions.discussion: Higher is not always better: an excess of current assets can signal idle inventory or slow collection, which is why the quick ratio is read alongside it.

wh.how: Current assets / Current liabilities
wh.why: It shows ability to meet short-term dues

questions.status: Ratio analysis remains a core tool in credit appraisal and is tested with the quick and cash ratios.
why_wrong: 1:1 implies no liquidity cushion.
1.5:1 would need current assets of ₹3,00,000.
3:1 would need current assets of ₹6,00,000.
questions.tip: Ratios are always expressed as the numerator over the denominator; check which figure sits on top before dividing.
questions.improve: Compute the quick ratio from the same data by removing inventory and prepaid expenses.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Accountancy, Part II

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.q: Under the Companies Act 2013, the minimum number of members required to form a private company is:
questions.history: The Companies Act 2013 requires a minimum of two members for a private company and seven for a public company, with a maximum of 200 for a private company.
questions.discussion: The Act also introduced the One Person Company, which allows a single member with limited liability, which is why option one is a deliberate trap.

wh.what: Minimum membership for a private company
wh.why: To distinguish private from public company structure

questions.status: The 2017 amendment simplified private company compliance, but membership thresholds stayed unchanged.
why_wrong: One is the requirement for an OPC, not a private company.
Five is not a statutory threshold under the Act.
Seven is the minimum for a public company.
questions.tip: Two for private, seven for public, one for OPC, 200 maximum for private. Four numbers cover this topic.
questions.improve: Learn the LLP Act 2008 thresholds alongside the company thresholds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The atomic number of an element equals the number of:
questions.history: Atomic number, denoted Z, counts protons in the nucleus and determines the element's identity in the modern periodic table.
questions.discussion: Mass number counts protons plus neutrons, so isotopes of an element share the atomic number but differ in mass number, which explains why isotopes behave identically in chemical reactions.

wh.who: Introduced by Moseley through X-ray studies
wh.why: It orders elements by nuclear charge, not atomic weight

questions.status: Moseley's ordering resolved anomalies in Mendeleev's weight-based table and is the basis of the modern periodic law.
why_wrong: Neutron count equals mass number minus atomic number.
Nucleons are protons plus neutrons together.
Valence electrons vary with the group and are not the atomic number.
questions.tip: Z is protons, A is protons plus neutrons, and charge is protons minus electrons.
questions.improve: Work out protons, neutrons and electrons for three ions of your choice.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Chemistry, Structure of Atom

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: A can do a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, they finish it in:
questions.history: Work problems are solved by adding rates, since one day of joint work equals the sum of each person's one-day output.
questions.discussion: A does 1/12 and B does 1/18 per day, giving 5/36 per day together, so the total time is 36/5, or 7.2 days.

wh.why: A guaranteed scoring area in arithmetic sections

questions.status: Exam variants include efficiency ratios and workers joining or leaving mid-task.
why_wrong: 6.5 days would need a faster combined rate than 5/36.
8 days comes from rounding up without computing the fraction.
9 days is roughly the average of the two times, a classic error.
questions.tip: Take the LCM of the days as total work, here 36 units, then convert each person to units per day.
questions.improve: Practise the LCM-unit method until you can do it without writing the fractions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.history: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble and changed 'unity of the Nation' to 'unity and integrity of the Nation'.
questions.discussion: The Kesavananda Bharati judgment held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended without altering its basic structure. The 42nd Amendment is the only one to have touched the Preamble.

wh.why: To formally commit the Republic to socialism and secularism

questions.status: Both words have been interpreted by courts as descriptive of the constitutional scheme, not as a licence for any single economic model.
why_wrong: These three words were in the original 1949 Preamble.
Justice, liberty and equality are original Preamble words.
Fraternity is original; dignity appears in the Fundamental Rights chapter, not the Preamble.
questions.tip: Only one amendment has ever changed the Preamble — the 42nd. Any question offering another number is a distractor.
questions.improve: Recite the Preamble and mark which words are original and which were added in 1976.
questions.source: Constitution of India, Preamble; 42nd Amendment Act 1976

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between the English East India Company and the forces of which Nawab?
questions.history: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey on 23 June 1757 with the help of Mir Jafar's defection, securing Bengal's revenues for the Company.
questions.discussion: Plassey was less a battle than a negotiated betrayal; the revenue surplus of Bengal then funded the Company's expansion across India.

wh.what: Battle that established Company power in Bengal
wh.why: Bengal's wealth and the misuse of trade privileges

questions.status: Often paired with Buxar (1764) in questions; Plassey began Company rule, Buxar legalised it with the Diwani grant of 1765.
why_wrong: Mir Qasim fought at Buxar in 1764 after being installed by the Company.
Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh was an ally at Buxar.
Alivardi Khan was Siraj-ud-Daulah's grandfather and predecessor.
questions.tip: Plassey 1757 gave power, Buxar 1764 gave legitimacy, Allahabad 1765 gave Diwani. Keep the chain.
questions.improve: Learn the three treaties — Allahabad 1765, Srirangapatnam 1792, Bassein 1802 — with their consequences.

questions.subject: Computer Fundamentals
questions.q: One byte is equal to how many bits?
questions.history: A byte of eight bits became the standard through IBM's System/360 in the 1960s, replacing earlier six and seven bit arrangements.
questions.discussion: Eight bits give 256 distinct values, enough for the ASCII character set, which is why character encoding and byte length are tied together.

wh.how: 1 byte = 8 bits
wh.why: Eight bits cover a full character set

questions.status: Modern systems still use 8-bit bytes, though word sizes have grown to 64 bits.
why_wrong: 4 bits is a nibble, half a byte.
16 bits is a word on older processors.
32 bits is a double word.
questions.tip: Learn the ladder: bit, nibble 4, byte 8, kilobyte 1024 bytes, and so on upward.
questions.improve: Convert 2 GB into bits to see how the units compound.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Chipko movement of 1973 was primarily associated with:
questions.history: Villagers in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, led by Sunderlal Bahuguna and Gaura Devi, hugged trees to prevent logging, giving the movement its name.
questions.discussion: Chipko linked forest rights to livelihoods and later fed into the 1980 Forest Conservation Act, which restricted diversion of forest land.

wh.who: Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt, Gaura Devi
wh.why: Commercial felling threatened village fuel, fodder and water

questions.status: Its principles continue in joint forest management and community forest rights under the 2006 Forest Rights Act.
why_wrong: Anti-dam protests are associated with the Narmada Bachao Andolan and Silent Valley.
Groundwater recharge is the work of the Tarun Bharat Sangh and similar groups.
Poaching is addressed by enforcement agencies, not social movements of this kind.
questions.tip: Three movements to keep apart: Chipko for forests, Narmada Bachao for dams, Appiko for forests in Karnataka.
questions.improve: Learn one leader, one State and one outcome for each environmental movement since 1970.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII, Politics in India since Independence

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.history: Shri Krishna Singh, known as Bihar Kesari, became the first Chief Minister in 1946 and held office until 1961, the longest tenure in the State's history.
questions.discussion: He combined the premiership with the revenue portfolio and drove land reform, including the abolition of zamindari, alongside the Bhoodan movement.

wh.why: Congress leadership in the pre-independence ministry continued into the State

questions.status: His tenure remains the benchmark for stability; Bihar has had more than 20 Chief Ministers since.
why_wrong: Rajendra Prasad was President of India, not Chief Minister.
Deep Narayan Singh served briefly in 1961.
Binodanand Jha was Chief Minister from 1961 to 1963.
questions.tip: Do not mix the Bihar Chief Minister with the first President, who was also a Bihar leader.
questions.improve: Make a list of Bihar Chief Ministers with tenure years for the last 30 years.

questions.subject: Psychology
questions.q: Classical conditioning was demonstrated by which experiment?
options: Pavlov's dogs salivating to a bell
questions.history: Pavlov paired a neutral stimulus, a bell, with food until the bell alone produced salivation, establishing the conditioned response.
questions.discussion: The other experiments map to distinct theories: operant conditioning, insight learning and observational learning, which is why examiners list them together.

wh.how: Pairing conditioned and unconditioned stimuli
wh.why: To explain how responses attach to new cues

questions.status: Classical conditioning underpins exposure therapy for phobias and aversion treatments.
why_wrong: Skinner's box demonstrates operant conditioning through reinforcement.
Kohler's chimpanzee demonstrates insight learning.
Bandura's bobo doll demonstrates observational learning.
questions.tip: One name, one theory: Pavlov classical, Skinner operant, Kohler insight, Bandura observational.
questions.improve: Draw the classical conditioning paradigm with UCS, CS, UCR and CR labelled.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.history: O negative red cells carry neither A nor B antigens nor the Rh D antigen, so they provoke no reaction in recipients of any group.
questions.discussion: The universal recipient is AB positive, which has no antibodies against any of these antigens. In practice plasma compatibility runs in the opposite direction to red cell compatibility.

wh.why: Antigen absence prevents agglutination
wh.how: ABO and Rh antigen systems together

questions.status: O negative is always in short supply and is the group blood banks appeal for most urgently.
why_wrong: AB positive is the universal recipient, the exact opposite.
A positive carries the A and Rh antigens.
B negative lacks the Rh antigen but carries B.
questions.tip: O negative gives to all, AB positive receives from all. Two facts, no confusion.
questions.improve: Draw a compatibility grid for the eight common blood groups.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Biology, Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Inflation caused by excess aggregate demand over available supply is called:
questions.history: Demand-pull inflation arises when spending grows faster than output, often described as too much money chasing too few goods.
questions.discussion: Cost-push inflation comes from the supply side, through wages, fuel or input prices. Policy responses differ, since demand compression can worsen a supply shock.

wh.why: To choose the right policy response
wh.how: Compare demand growth with output growth

questions.status: India's recent episodes have mixed imported fuel costs with food supply shocks, making classification difficult.
why_wrong: Cost-push comes from rising input or wage costs.
Imported inflation arrives through global prices and the exchange rate.
Structural inflation reflects supply bottlenecks in specific sectors.
questions.tip: Demand-pull is too much money, cost-push is too costly inputs. Ask which side of the market moved first.
questions.improve: Note one policy instrument suited to each inflation type.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Black cotton soil of the Deccan is best described as which soil type?
questions.history: Regur or black soil formed from weathered Deccan trap basalt, is rich in iron, lime and magnesia, and retains moisture well, suiting cotton.
questions.discussion: Its dark colour comes from titanium and humus content, and its self-ploughing behaviour on drying and wetting is a favourite exam detail.

wh.what: Black cotton soil, also called regur
wh.why: Derived from basaltic lava of the Deccan traps
wh.how: High clay content makes it swell and crack

questions.status: Heavily used for cotton and soybean; poor drainage and low nitrogen are its main limits.
why_wrong: Alluvial soil is transported by rivers, found in the northern plains and deltas.
Laterite soil forms in high rainfall leaching zones such as Kerala and Karnataka.
Arid soils occur in Rajasthan and lack humus.
questions.tip: Match soil to parent material: regur from basalt, laterite from leaching, alluvial from river deposits, red soil from crystalline rock.
questions.improve: Prepare a soil table with region, crop and one limitation each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Kalinga war, which turned Ashoka towards Dhamma, is described in which Major Rock Edict?
questions.history: Major Rock Edict XIII records the conquest of Kalinga in the eighth year of Ashoka's reign, around 261 BCE, and his remorse at the slaughter.
questions.discussion: The edict also names five Hellenistic kings as recipients of his Dhamma missions, which is how historians date and locate his diplomatic reach.

wh.what: Account of the Kalinga war and remorse
wh.why: To announce a shift from conquest by arms to conquest by Dhamma

questions.status: Ashokan edicts remain the earliest deciphered Indian inscriptions, read after James Prinsep's 1837 breakthrough.
why_wrong: Rock Edict II mentions medical facilities for men and animals.
Rock Edict X praises Dhamma administration.
Rock Edict XI sets out the policy of Dhamma gifts to all sects.
questions.tip: Remember XIII as the unlucky war edict: thirteen matches the year of the Kalinga campaign in the eighth regnal year narrative.
questions.improve: List five Ashokan edicts with their subject in one column; exams rarely go beyond that list.
questions.source: Major Rock Edict XIII; NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the next term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.history: The series follows n(n+1) for n = 1, 2, 3 and so on, giving products of consecutive numbers.
questions.discussion: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10 and then 12, so the next term is 30 + 12 = 42, a second and faster route to the same answer.

wh.how: Check first differences, then second differences
wh.why: A high-frequency reasoning question

questions.status: Modern papers mix two interleaved series to raise difficulty.
why_wrong: 36 assumes a constant difference of 6, which breaks at the second term.
40 does not fit either the difference pattern or n(n+1).
44 would need a difference of 14.
questions.tip: When differences grow by 2 each time, the underlying rule is usually a quadratic such as n(n+1).
questions.improve: Practise ten series mixing squares, cubes, primes and alternating patterns.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which number does not belong: 121, 144, 169, 190?
questions.history: 121, 144 and 169 are the squares of 11, 12 and 13, while 190 is not a perfect square.
questions.discussion: Odd-one-out questions usually rest on one property shared by all but one option; here perfect squares is that property, and checking the square root settles it in seconds.

wh.how: Test squares, cubes, primes and divisibility
wh.why: Tests pattern recognition speed

questions.status: Banking papers often use letter-position or Roman numeral properties instead of arithmetic ones.
why_wrong: 121 is 11 squared.
144 is 12 squared.
169 is 13 squared.
questions.tip: Memorise squares up to 30 and cubes up to 15; most number-based odd-one-out questions collapse instantly.
questions.improve: Keep a written chart of squares 1 to 30 and revise it daily for a week.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: An article bought for ₹480 is sold for ₹552. The profit percentage is:
questions.history: Profit percentage is always calculated on cost price unless the question says otherwise.
questions.discussion: Profit is 72 on a cost of 480, and 72/480 gives exactly 15 per cent, which is the clean answer examiners expect.

wh.how: (SP - CP) / CP × 100
wh.why: Core commercial arithmetic

questions.status: Higher-level variants involve marked price, successive discounts and dishonest dealing.
why_wrong: 12% would need a profit of about 58.
18% would need a selling price near 566.
20% would need a selling price of 576.
questions.tip: Divide profit by cost, never by selling price. Most wrong options are built on the wrong denominator.
questions.improve: Do five problems where the profit is on selling price, since those invert the formula.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Barauni oil refinery is located in which district of Bihar?
questions.history: The Barauni refinery, commissioned in 1964 by Indian Oil, sits in Begusarai district and was built with Soviet technical assistance.
questions.discussion: It is fed by the crude pipeline from Haldia and anchors the Barauni industrial belt, which also includes a thermal power station and fertiliser units.

wh.what: Oil refinery of Indian Oil Corporation
wh.why: To process crude for eastern India's growing demand

questions.status: Capacity has been expanded to about 6 million tonnes a year, with a polypropylene unit added.
why_wrong: Barauni is a town inside Begusarai, not in Patna district.
Bhagalpur has no refinery.
Purnia has no refinery.
questions.tip: Barauni town sits inside Begusarai district — the district name is the answer, not the town name.
questions.improve: List Bihar's major industrial units with their districts.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One word for 'a person who talks too much':
questions.history: Garrulous comes from the Latin garrire, to chatter, and describes someone habitually talkative about trivial matters.
questions.discussion: All four options relate to speech, but three describe saying little, which makes this a classic grouping trap.

wh.how: Check the direction of meaning before choosing
wh.why: Vocabulary density question

questions.status: Exams prefer words with Latin roots that can be reasoned out.
why_wrong: Taciturn means habitually silent.
Reticent means reserved in speech.
Laconic means using very few words.
questions.tip: Sort the options into talkative and silent groups first; the answer is then a one-in-four choice inside one group.
questions.improve: Build a one-word substitution list of 100 items grouped by theme.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'abundant'.
questions.history: Abundant comes from the Latin abundare, to overflow, and means present in large quantity.
questions.discussion: The three wrong options are near-synonyms of each other, which is a reliable signal in antonym-style distractors.

wh.how: Substitute the word into a sentence and test the sense
wh.why: Vocabulary carries several marks in SSC and banking English

questions.status: Modern papers prefer contextual vocabulary over isolated word lists.
why_wrong: Scarce is the antonym.
Rare means uncommon, close to the opposite.
Limited suggests restriction rather than quantity.
questions.tip: When three options cluster as synonyms of each other, the fourth is usually the answer.
questions.improve: Learn vocabulary in antonym pairs; it doubles retention for the same effort.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.q: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which need sits at the base?
questions.history: Maslow placed physiological needs such as food, water and shelter at the base, arguing that higher needs motivate only after the lower ones are reasonably met.
questions.discussion: The order runs physiological, safety, social, esteem and self-actualisation. Organisations typically satisfy the lower two through wages and job security and the upper three through recognition and autonomy.

wh.why: To explain what motivates behaviour at different stages
wh.how: Lower needs are satisfied before higher ones

questions.status: Modern research treats the hierarchy as flexible rather than rigid, but it remains the standard teaching model.
why_wrong: Esteem is the fourth level.
Safety is the second level.
Self-actualisation is the top level.
questions.tip: Remember the ladder by its first letters: Physiological, Safety, Social, Esteem, Self-actualisation.
questions.improve: Write one workplace example of how each level is met.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Business Studies, Chapter on Directing

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: When demand does not change at all with a change in price, price elasticity of demand equals:
questions.history: Perfectly inelastic demand has an elasticity of zero and a vertical demand curve, typical of life-saving medicines.
questions.discussion: Elasticity measures responsiveness, so no response means zero. At the other extreme, perfectly elastic demand has infinite elasticity and a horizontal curve.

wh.how: Percentage change in quantity over percentage change in price
wh.why: It drives pricing and tax incidence

questions.status: Tax policy uses elasticity: goods with inelastic demand carry more of the tax burden and generate stable revenue.
why_wrong: Unit elasticity means quantity changes proportionally, not not at all.
Infinite elasticity means any price rise destroys all demand.
Any positive value implies some response.
questions.tip: Zero means no response, one means proportional, infinity means any price change wipes out demand.
questions.improve: Draw all five elasticity cases with their curve shapes.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: The average of the first 20 natural numbers is:
questions.history: The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)/2, so the average is (n+1)/2.
questions.discussion: For n = 20, the sum is 210 and the average 10.5. A quick sanity check: the average of 1 to 20 must sit between 10 and 11.

wh.what: Average of a natural number series
wh.why: A standard speed-calculation question

questions.status: Exam variants ask for the average of first n even, odd or square numbers.
why_wrong: 10 is the average of the first 19 natural numbers, a common off-by-one error.
11 would be the average of 1 to 21.
20.5 is the average of 1 to 40.
questions.tip: For consecutive numbers, the average is simply the midpoint of the first and last terms.
questions.improve: Memorise the sum formulas for natural numbers, squares and cubes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Fiscal deficit is best defined as:
options: Total expenditure minus total revenue receipts
Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
Interest payments as a share of GDP
questions.history: Fiscal deficit measures the government's total borrowing requirement, covering both revenue and capital spending gaps.
questions.discussion: Revenue deficit shows consumption shortfall, while fiscal deficit includes capital spending, which is why a government can run a fiscal deficit to build assets.

wh.why: It shows how much the government must borrow to meet spending
wh.how: Total expenditure minus total receipts other than borrowings
wh.who: Reported by the Controller General of Accounts monthly

questions.status: India's fiscal consolidation path targets a deficit below 4.5 per cent of GDP in the medium term under the FRBM framework.
why_wrong: That would overstate the deficit by ignoring non-debt capital receipts such as disinvestment.
That is the revenue deficit.
That is the interest payments ratio, a debt sustainability indicator.
questions.tip: Remember the family: revenue deficit, effective revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, primary deficit. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
questions.improve: Compute all four deficits from one set of hypothetical budget numbers.

questions.subject: Networking
questions.q: The default port number for HTTP is:
questions.history: HTTP uses port 80 by default, while HTTPS uses 443 with TLS layered on top.
questions.discussion: Port numbers route traffic to the right service on a single IP address, so a server can run web, mail and file services simultaneously.

wh.how: IANA assigns ports 0 to 1023 to standard services
wh.why: One IP address must serve many services

questions.status: Browsers now default to HTTPS on 443, and port 80 often redirects there.
why_wrong: 21 is FTP.
25 is SMTP for mail transfer.
443 is HTTPS.
questions.tip: Memorise five ports: 21 FTP, 25 SMTP, 53 DNS, 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS.
questions.improve: Note the difference between TCP and UDP with one example each.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which Indian State has the longest coastline?
questions.history: Gujarat's coastline of about 1,600 km, including the Gulf of Kachchh and Gulf of Khambhat, is the longest of any Indian State.
questions.discussion: The indented coast with gulfs, creeks and the Kathiawar peninsula gives Gujarat more than twice the coastline of the next State.

wh.why: Deep inlets and peninsular projections
wh.how: About 1,600 km, roughly 20 per cent of India's total

questions.status: Central to port-led development, with Mundra, Kandla and the Vadhavan project.
why_wrong: Tamil Nadu's coast is about 1,076 km.
Andhra Pradesh's coast is about 975 km.
Maharashtra's coast is about 720 km.
questions.tip: Coastline order: Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra.
questions.improve: Note the nine coastal States and four coastal UTs in order of length.
questions.source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways; NCERT Class XI

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.history: The INC's first session was held in Bombay in December 1885 with Womesh Chandra Bannerjee as President and 72 delegates; A.O. Hume was the moving force behind its founding.
questions.discussion: The early Congress was a moderate body seeking representation in councils, a phase later challenged by Tilak's extremists and then by Gandhi's mass politics.

wh.why: To create an all-India political platform

questions.status: The party led the freedom struggle and became the dominant political force in independent India.
why_wrong: A.O. Hume was the founder-organiser, not the first President.
Dadabhai Naoroji was President in 1886, 1893 and 1906.
Badruddin Tyabji was the third President, in 1887.
questions.tip: Distinguish founder, first President and first Muslim President — Hume, Bannerjee, Tyabji.
questions.improve: Keep a list of Congress sessions with year, venue and President for 1885 to 1947 highlights.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII, Modern India; INC records

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: President's Rule in a State is imposed under which Article?
questions.history: Article 356 allows the President to assume State functions when the constitutional machinery fails, on a report from the Governor.
questions.discussion: The S.R. Bommai judgment of 1994 made the power justiciable, required a floor test where majority was in doubt, and ended the routine misuse of Article 356 during the 1970s and 1980s.

wh.what: Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
wh.why: To preserve constitutional governance in the State
wh.how: Proclamation must be approved by Parliament within two months

questions.status: Use has fallen sharply after Bommai; proclamations now typically follow loss of majority and a floor test.
why_wrong: Article 352 is the national emergency provision.
Article 360 covers financial emergency, never invoked.
Article 365 covers a State failing to comply with Union directions.
questions.tip: Emergency articles in order: 352 national, 356 State, 360 financial. Remember 3-5-6 as the ladder downward.
questions.improve: Read the S.R. Bommai ratio once and note the three tests the Court laid down.
questions.source: Constitution of India, Article 356; S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)

questions.subject: Statistics
questions.q: The empirical relationship between mean, median and mode is:
questions.history: Karl Pearson's empirical relation for moderately skewed distributions is Mode equals three times Median minus twice the Mean.
questions.discussion: The formula explains why the mean is pulled furthest by skewness while the median stays in the middle, a point examiners test through numerical problems.

wh.why: To estimate one average when the other two are known

questions.status: The relation is approximate and holds best for moderately skewed unimodal distributions.
why_wrong: The coefficients are swapped, which gives wrong values for any skewed data.
This rearranges the formula incorrectly.
This is a different rearrangement that does not follow from Pearson's relation.
questions.tip: Say it as a sentence: three medians minus two means gives the mode. The 3-2 order is the whole formula.
questions.improve: Test the relation on a small dataset and note the approximation error.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Statistics, Measures of Central Tendency

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens is also known as a:
questions.history: A convex lens is thicker at the centre, so parallel rays converge to a real focus; a concave lens is thinner at the centre and diverges rays.
questions.discussion: The sign convention follows from this: focal length is positive for a convex lens in the Cartesian system, which is why the lens formula gives a positive image distance for real images.

wh.how: Centre thickness decides convergence or divergence
wh.why: Convergence is the basis of cameras, eyes and magnifiers

questions.status: Modern optics uses the same geometry in fibre collimators and camera lens stacks.
why_wrong: A diverging lens is concave, thinner at the centre.
Plano is a surface description, not a lens class.
Cylindrical lenses correct astigmatism and describe shape, not convergence.
questions.tip: Convex converges, concave diverges. The letter C repeats and so does the property pair.
questions.improve: Trace three rays through a convex lens and locate the image for an object beyond 2F.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: A Money Bill is defined under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.history: Article 110 defines a Money Bill as one dealing only with taxation, borrowing, the Consolidated Fund, appropriation of money or audit of Union accounts.
questions.discussion: The Speaker certifies a Bill as a Money Bill, and the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject it, only recommend within 14 days. The certification power was examined in the Rojer Mathew and Mohd. Saeed Siddiqui line of cases.

wh.what: Definition and scope of a Money Bill
wh.who: Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies it
wh.why: Financial legislation must stay with the directly elected House
wh.how: Lok Sabha passes it; Rajya Sabha has 14 days to recommend

questions.status: Live debate: whether the Speaker's certification is final or open to judicial review in limited circumstances.
why_wrong: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting to resolve deadlock between the Houses.
Article 112 is the annual Financial Statement, the Budget.
Article 117 covers financial Bills other than Money Bills.
questions.tip: Learn 108 to 117 as one cluster — joint sitting, Money Bill, Budget, financial Bills, and the Appropriation process all sit together.
questions.improve: Write a table of Money Bill vs Financial Bill (I and II) vs Ordinary Bill with the role of each House.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The law of demand states that, other things remaining constant, price and quantity demanded are:
questions.history: The law of demand rests on the income and substitution effects: a higher price reduces purchasing power and pushes buyers towards substitutes.
questions.discussion: Exceptions include Giffen goods, where a price rise increases demand among the very poor, and goods bought for conspicuous display, where price signals status.

wh.why: Income and substitution effects
wh.how: Shown as a downward sloping demand curve

questions.status: Behavioural economics has qualified the law, but it remains the foundation of microeconomic teaching.
why_wrong: A direct relationship describes supply, not demand.
Unrelated demand curves are vertical, a special case, not the law.
The law applies broadly, not only to luxuries.
questions.tip: Demand slopes down, supply slopes up. Every curve question begins with that picture.
questions.improve: Learn the two exceptions to the law with an Indian example each.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Vikramshila University was founded by which Pala ruler?
questions.history: Dharmapala founded Vikramshila in the eighth century near Bhagalpur, and it became a rival centre to Nalanda, especially strong in tantric Buddhist studies.
questions.discussion: Its ruins at Antichak in Bhagalpur district were excavated from the 1960s, revealing a large cruciform stupa and a monastery laid out on a square plan.
questions.status: Protected by the ASI; proposals to develop it as a heritage tourism circuit are ongoing.
why_wrong: Gopala was the first Pala ruler and founder of the dynasty.
Devapala expanded the empire but did not found Vikramshila.
Mahipala ruled much later, in the eleventh century.
questions.tip: Gopala founded the dynasty, Dharmapala founded Vikramshila — the alliteration of D is your memory hook.
questions.improve: Learn the Pala rulers in order with one achievement each.
questions.source: ASI Antichak excavations; NCERT Themes in Indian History

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.q: In a sole proprietorship, the liability of the owner is:
options: Limited to the value of stock
questions.history: A sole proprietorship has no separate legal identity, so business debts can be recovered from the proprietor's personal assets.
questions.discussion: This unlimited liability is the main reason such firms struggle to raise finance, and it is why limited liability partnership and company forms exist.

wh.why: No separate legal entity from the owner
wh.how: Creditors can proceed against personal property

questions.status: One Person Company under the Companies Act 2013 offers limited liability to a single entrepreneur, which is the modern alternative.
why_wrong: Limited liability is a feature of companies and LLPs.
Liability is not capped by stock value.
Creditors do not share liability; they enforce it.
questions.tip: Separate legal entity and limited liability always travel together. If there is no separate entity, liability is unlimited.
questions.improve: Compare sole proprietorship, partnership, LLP and company on five parameters in one table.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Business Studies, Forms of Business Organisation

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Nalanda Mahavihara, the ancient centre of learning, was founded under the patronage of which Gupta ruler?
questions.history: Nalanda was established in the fifth century CE under Kumaragupta I, and seals and inscriptions credit him as its founder; it flourished for about 700 years.
questions.discussion: Hiuen Tsang studied there under Silabhadra and left a detailed account of its monastic organisation, which historians use to reconstruct its curriculum.

wh.why: Gupta patronage of Buddhist scholasticism

questions.status: A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2016; the modern Nalanda University at Rajgir was revived by an Act of Parliament in 2010.
why_wrong: Samudragupta is known for his conquests recorded in the Allahabad pillar inscription.
Chandragupta II is associated with the Mehrauli iron pillar and the Udayagiri caves.
Skandagupta ruled later, during Huna invasions.
questions.tip: Pala rulers founded Vikramshila and Odantapuri; the Guptas founded Nalanda. Keep the dynasty-founder pair straight.
questions.improve: List the three great mahaviharas of Bihar with their founders and locations.
questions.source: ASI; NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They cancelled the match.'
options: The match is cancelled by them.
The match was cancelled by them.
The match were cancelled by them.
questions.history: The passive is formed with the appropriate form of be plus the past participle, keeping the tense of the active sentence.
questions.discussion: The active verb is simple past, so the passive needs 'was' with a singular subject, giving 'The match was cancelled by them'.

wh.how: Object becomes subject, verb becomes be plus past participle
wh.why: Grammar transformation questions appear every year

questions.status: Higher-level papers ask for passive forms of sentences with modals.
why_wrong: 'Is cancelled' changes the tense to present.
'Has cancelled' is active and grammatically incomplete here.
'Were cancelled' mismatches the singular subject.
questions.tip: Keep the tense, change the voice. Write the tense of the original first, then build the passive around it.
questions.improve: Convert ten active sentences across all tenses into passive voice.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Gross National Product (GNP) equals GDP plus:
questions.history: GNP counts the output of a country's residents wherever they are, so it adds net factor income from abroad to GDP.
questions.discussion: For India, net factor income from abroad is usually negative, which is why GNP is lower than GDP. Adjusting GNP for depreciation gives Net National Product.

wh.how: GNP = GDP + NFIA
wh.why: To distinguish location of production from ownership

questions.status: India reports GVA at basic prices as the headline supply-side measure alongside GDP.
why_wrong: Depreciation converts GNP into NNP, not GDP into GNP.
Indirect taxes enter the market price versus factor cost distinction.
Subsidies also affect factor cost adjustments, not the national versus domestic split.
questions.tip: Domestic means inside the border, National means by residents. The gap is factor income from abroad.
questions.improve: Compute NNP at factor cost from GDP at market price using a small set of numbers.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Tiger was launched in which year?
questions.history: Project Tiger began on 1 April 1973 at Jim Corbett National Park with nine reserves, after the 1972 Wildlife Protection Act gave the legal framework.
questions.discussion: The project moved tiger conservation from sport hunting to habitat management with core-buffer zoning, and the National Tiger Conservation Authority now oversees it.

wh.where: Started at Jim Corbett, now across 50 plus reserves
wh.why: Tiger numbers had collapsed to about 1,800 by 1972

questions.status: The 2022 All India Tiger Estimation placed the population at about 3,682, the largest in the world.
why_wrong: 1972 is the Wildlife Protection Act, the enabling law.
1980 is associated with the Forest Conservation Act.
1992 is when Project Elephant was launched.
questions.tip: Pair year and instrument: 1972 Wildlife Act, 1973 Project Tiger, 1980 Forest Conservation Act, 1992 Project Elephant.
questions.improve: Note the difference between a national park, a sanctuary and a reserve under the 1972 Act.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
1. Cripps Mission
2. Cabinet Mission
3. Wavell Plan
4. Mountbatten Plan
questions.history: The Cripps Mission came in 1942, the Wavell Plan and the Simla Conference in 1945, the Cabinet Mission in 1946, and the Mountbatten Plan in June 1947.
questions.discussion: The sequence tracks the collapsing British position: wartime offers of dominion status, then post-war attempts to hold the centre together, then the decision to partition and leave.

wh.what: Order of British missions and plans
wh.why: Each followed a shift in the British strategic position

questions.status: The Cabinet Mission Plan's grouping scheme remains central to debates on why partition became unavoidable.
why_wrong: This places the Cabinet Mission before the Wavell Plan, which is wrong.
The Cripps Mission came first, in 1942.
The Mountbatten Plan came after the Cabinet Mission.
questions.tip: Anchor on two dates: Cripps 1942 (during the war) and Mountbatten 1947 (the last one). The middle two are Wavell then Cabinet.
questions.improve: Make a timeline of 1940 to 1947 with one line per event.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: A firm has a current ratio of 2.5 and a quick ratio of 1.5. If its current liabilities are ₹4,00,000, the value of inventory is:
questions.history: The quick ratio removes inventory and prepaid expenses from current assets, so the gap between the two ratios isolates stock.
questions.discussion: Current assets are 2.5 × 4,00,000 = 10,00,000. Quick assets are 1.5 × 4,00,000 = 6,00,000. The difference, 4,00,000, is inventory.

wh.what: Derivation of inventory from two ratios
wh.how: CA = CR × CL, quick assets = QR × CL, inventory = CA − quick assets
wh.why: A standard two-step numerical in ratio analysis

questions.status: Ind AS presentation may separate inventories into raw material, WIP and finished goods, but the arithmetic is unchanged.
why_wrong: ₹3,00,000 comes from a quick ratio of 1.75.
₹5,00,000 would need a quick ratio of 1.25.
₹6,00,000 is the quick assets figure, not inventory.
questions.tip: Write both equations with the same denominator first. The subtraction then gives inventory in one line.
questions.improve: Solve five problems that give two ratios and ask for a balance sheet item.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Accountancy, Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The slogan 'Do or Die' is associated with which movement?
questions.history: At the Gowalia Tank session of August 1942, Gandhi gave the Quit India call with the slogan 'Do or Die', demanding an orderly British withdrawal.
questions.discussion: The movement saw the arrest of the entire Congress leadership, spontaneous mass action, and the parallel government experiments at Ballia, Tamluk and Satara.

wh.who: Gandhi and the Congress Working Committee
wh.why: The fall of Southeast Asia made British withdrawal look urgent

questions.status: Cited as the final mass upsurge before independence; several local parallel governments are studied as evidence of rural self-rule.
why_wrong: Non-Cooperation 1920-22 was built on boycott and the Tilak Swaraj Fund.
Civil Disobedience 1930 followed the Eleven Point ultimatum.
Swadeshi 1905 was the boycott of partition of Bengal.
questions.tip: Three slogans, three movements: Inquilab Zindabad with 1930, Do or Die with 1942, Jai Hind as the final salute.
questions.improve: Learn the parallel governments of 1942 with their districts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oxidation in terms of electron transfer means:
questions.history: The modern electronic definition is OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain of electrons, which replaced earlier oxygen and hydrogen based definitions.
questions.discussion: Because electrons lost by one species must be gained by another, oxidation and reduction always occur together, which is why the term redox is used.

wh.how: OIL RIG
wh.why: It generalises oxidation beyond reactions with oxygen

questions.status: The definition now underpins electrochemistry, corrosion science and battery design.
why_wrong: Gain of electrons is reduction.
Proton transfer describes acid-base reactions, not redox.
Neutrons are not exchanged in chemical reactions.
questions.tip: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain. Learn the mnemonic and you will never invert it under pressure.
questions.improve: Identify the oxidising and reducing agents in three reactions.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Chemistry, Redox Reactions

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The account 'Indica' was written by which Greek ambassador to the Mauryan court?
questions.history: Megasthenes, ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at Chandragupta Maurya's court, wrote Indica describing society, administration and the capital Pataliputra.
questions.discussion: The original is lost and survives only in fragments quoted by later writers, so historians treat its colourful claims cautiously while still mining them for administration details.

wh.why: To inform the Seleucid court about its eastern neighbour

questions.status: Fragments are used in NCERT and in epigraphy courses as a foreign-eye source on the Mauryas.
why_wrong: Fa-Hien was a Chinese pilgrim of the Gupta period.
Kautilya wrote the Arthashastra, not a foreign account.
Al-Biruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote on eleventh-century India.
questions.tip: Foreign accounts in order: Megasthenes (Mauryan), Fa-Hien (Gupta), Hiuen Tsang (Harsha), Al-Biruni (Ghaznavid).
questions.improve: Note which foreign account is useful for which period; that alone solves elimination questions.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part I

questions.subject: English
questions.q: 'Hamlet' was written by:
questions.history: Shakespeare wrote Hamlet around 1600, and it was published in the Second Quarto of 1604 with the fuller text.
questions.discussion: Marlowe and Jonson were contemporaries of Shakespeare, which is why their names appear as distractors in every literature paper on the period.

wh.why: Studied for its soliloquies and revenge plot structure

questions.status: The play remains the most performed and most adapted work in the English canon.
why_wrong: Marlowe wrote Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine.
Milton wrote Paradise Lost.
Jonson wrote Volpone and The Alchemist.
questions.tip: Group Elizabethan playwrights by their best-known work; one title each is enough for identification.
questions.improve: Learn five Shakespeare plays with genre and approximate year.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI English; Arden Shakespeare editions

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: According to Ohm's law, the relationship between potential difference and current at constant temperature is:
options: V is inversely proportional to I
questions.history: Ohm's law states that at constant temperature the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, giving V = IR.
