questions.discussion: The constant of proportionality is resistance, and materials that obey this relationship are called ohmic. Semiconductors and filament lamps deviate, which is why the law is stated with the temperature condition.

wh.how: V = IR
wh.why: It allows circuit design by arithmetic

questions.status: Ohm's law holds for metallic conductors at constant temperature and fails for non-ohmic devices.
why_wrong: Power dissipated is proportional to I², not voltage itself.
Inverse proportionality would mean higher voltage gives lower current.
Voltage and current are not independent in a resistor.
questions.tip: Read the law as a sentence: more voltage pushes more current through the same resistance.
questions.improve: Plot V against I for a resistor and for a bulb and compare the slopes.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are red. Conclusion: Some pens are red. The conclusion is:
questions.history: In syllogisms a conclusion follows only if it must be true in every possible arrangement consistent with the statements.
questions.discussion: The red books may or may not be the books that are pens, so the conclusion is only a possibility, not a certainty. That distinction is the whole test.

wh.how: Check whether any arrangement makes the statements true but the conclusion false
wh.why: Tests strict logical rather than everyday reasoning

questions.status: Banking papers add possibility cases with 'some not' statements to increase difficulty.
why_wrong: It is not definitely true because a valid counter-arrangement exists.
It is not definitely false either, since one arrangement makes it true.
It can be evaluated, so this option is a cop-out.
questions.tip: Draw the minimum overlap Venn diagram; if a second diagram can break the conclusion, it is only a possibility.
questions.improve: Practise the standard three-figure method for 'all', 'some' and 'no' statements.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Chilika Lake, India's largest brackish water lagoon, lies in which State?
questions.history: Chilika, on the Odisha coast, is a lagoon separated from the Bay of Bengal by a sand bar, and was designated a Ramsar site in 1981.
questions.discussion: Its salinity fluctuates with the opening and closing of the sea mouth, which drives the lagoon's fishery and its famous Irrawaddy dolphin population.

wh.where: Puri, Khordha and Ganjam districts, Odisha
wh.why: Formed by coastal sediment deposition closing a bay
wh.how: Fed by the Daya, Bhargavi and Makra rivers

questions.status: Eutrophication and shrimp-farm pressure are persistent threats; the sea mouth is dredged periodically.
why_wrong: West Bengal's Sundarbans is a delta, not a lagoon.
Andhra Pradesh has Pulicat on its border with Tamil Nadu, which is smaller.
Tamil Nadu's Pulicat portion is smaller than Chilika.
questions.tip: Lagoon pairs: Chilika in Odisha, Pulicat between Andhra and Tamil Nadu, Vembanad in Kerala.
questions.improve: Mark India's Ramsar sites on an outline map by State.
questions.source: Ramsar Sites Information Service; NCERT Class XI

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of power is:
questions.history: One watt is one joule of work done per second, named after James Watt, whose steam engine improvements made the measure commercially important.
questions.discussion: Power is a rate, which is why time appears in its definition. Electrical power uses the same unit, computed as V times I.

wh.how: P = W/t = VI
wh.why: To compare devices that do the same work at different speeds

questions.status: Household consumption is billed in kilowatt-hours, which is energy, not power.
why_wrong: Newton measures force.
Joule measures energy or work.
Coulomb measures electric charge.
questions.tip: Watt is per second, joule is the amount. Any 'per unit time' phrase points to power.
questions.improve: Convert a 100 W bulb's one-month usage into kilowatt-hours.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Physics, Work Energy and Power

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a keyword in C?
questions.history: C has 32 keywords in the C89 standard, and main is a function name defined by the programmer, not a reserved word.
questions.discussion: Because main is not reserved, a programmer could technically use it as a variable name, though doing so would break the program's entry point and is poor practice.

wh.how: Check the reserved word list for the standard
wh.why: Keywords cannot be used as identifiers

questions.status: C11 and C17 added a few keywords such as _Static_assert and _Generic, but main remains an identifier.
why_wrong: static is a storage class keyword.
volatile is a type qualifier keyword.
register is a storage class keyword.
questions.tip: main is a function, not a keyword. If a question lists it among keywords, it is usually the answer.
questions.improve: Memorise the 32 C keywords by grouping them into storage, type and control categories.
questions.source: BCA C Programming syllabus; ISO C standard

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: A 60 litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3. How much water does it contain?
questions.history: In a fixed ratio, each part equals total divided by the number of parts, so one part here is 6 litres.
questions.discussion: Water is 3 parts of 6 litres, that is 18 litres, and milk is 42 litres; the two add to 60, which is the quickest check.

wh.how: Total / sum of ratio terms × required term
wh.why: Base skill for alligation problems

questions.status: Exam variants add or replace a quantity and ask for the new ratio.
why_wrong: 15 litres comes from dividing 60 by 4, the wrong number of parts.
21 litres is the milk-to-water confusion in reverse.
24 litres comes from treating water as 4 parts.
questions.tip: Always convert the ratio to a total number of parts first, then multiply. Then verify by adding both components back to the total.
questions.improve: Practise replacement problems, where a portion is removed and refilled.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Patna Kalam style of painting is best known for depicting:
questions.history: Patna Kalam grew in the eighteenth century after Mughal artists moved east, and it is known for small-scale watercolours of traders, craftsmen, festivals and household life.
questions.discussion: Art historians call it Company painting or the Patna Qalam, distinguished from court art by its ordinary subjects and cheaper materials for a new bazaar market.

wh.why: Mughal decline pushed artists towards local patronage

questions.status: Examples are held in the Patna Museum and the Victoria and Albert Museum.
why_wrong: Mughal court scenes belong to the Mughal miniature tradition, which Patna Kalam moved away from.
Religious icons were painted, but they do not define the style's character.
Himalayan landscapes belong to later Company and Bengal School painters.
questions.tip: Patna Kalam equals ordinary life; Mughal miniature equals court life. The subject is the giveaway.
questions.improve: Learn three artists associated with Patna Kalam and one painting each.
questions.source: Patna Museum; NCERT Class XII Fine Arts

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Which leader led the 1857 revolt in the Jagdishpur region of Bihar?
questions.history: Babu Veer Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur, an octogenarian zamindar of Arrah, led the revolt in Bihar from 1857 to 1858 and died shortly after defeating a British force.
questions.discussion: His campaign combined guerrilla tactics with coordination with Nana Saheb's forces, and the Amar Singh episode at Jagdishpur became a local legend of resistance.

wh.who: Kunwar Singh and his brother Amar Singh

questions.status: Veer Kunwar Singh University in Arrah and an annual fair commemorate him.
why_wrong: Pir Ali Khan was a religious figure, not a leader of this revolt.
Ahmadullah Shah led in Awadh and Rohilkhand.
Nana Saheb led at Kanpur.
questions.tip: Map 1857 leaders to places: Kanpur Nana Saheb, Jhansi Lakshmibai, Awadh Begum Hazrat Mahal, Bihar Kunwar Singh, Delhi Bakht Khan.
questions.improve: Note three reasons why the 1857 revolt failed to become a national war.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: What is the maximum sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.history: Article 80 caps the Rajya Sabha at 250 members — up to 238 representing States and Union Territories and 12 nominated by the President for special knowledge.
questions.discussion: The fourth Schedule allocates seats among States, and the actual membership stays below the ceiling because seats follow population and State allocation rather than filling every slot.

wh.how: 238 elected indirectly by MLAs plus 12 nominated
wh.why: To give States a voice and provide a revising chamber
wh.when: Members serve six-year terms, one-third retiring every two years

questions.status: Current strength is 245; the 12 nominated seats have occasionally stayed vacant for long periods.
why_wrong: 238 is only the elected component, not the ceiling.
245 is the present actual strength, not the constitutional maximum.
252 is above the constitutional limit and appears nowhere in Article 80.
questions.tip: Separate the ceiling from the actual: Rajya Sabha 250 ceiling, 245 present; Lok Sabha 552 ceiling, 543 present.
questions.improve: Write the composition of both Houses with ceilings, present strength and term lengths in one table.
questions.source: Constitution of India, Article 80 and Fourth Schedule

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Dandi March of 1930 was launched primarily to protest against which tax?
questions.history: Gandhi walked 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi over 24 days in March-April 1930 and made salt at the shore, defying the government monopoly.
questions.discussion: Salt was chosen because it touched every household, making the protest legible to the poorest Indian and turning a local act into a national movement.

wh.what: Civil disobedience against the salt law
wh.who: Gandhi with 78 volunteers at the start
wh.why: The salt tax hit every household regardless of income

questions.status: Commemorated annually as the Dandi March anniversary; the site is a national memorial.
why_wrong: Land revenue was the focus of peasant movements such as Champaran and Kheda.
Income tax was not the issue; the campaign targeted a mass consumption item.
Cloth excise was tied to the boycott of foreign cloth, a different strand of the movement.
questions.tip: For every Gandhian movement, fix the year, place and the specific law — Champaran 1917, Kheda 1918, Khilafat 1919, Non-cooperation 1920, Dandi 1930, Quit India 1942.
questions.improve: Draw a one-page timeline of 1915 to 1947 with one trigger per movement.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar's only tiger reserve, is located in which district?
questions.history: Valmiki Tiger Reserve in Pashchim Champaran was declared a tiger reserve in 1994 and covers the Terai-Bhabar tract along the Gandak and Pandai rivers.
questions.discussion: It forms part of the Terai Arc Landscape linking Nepal's Chitwan with Indian reserves, which is why tiger movement across the border is monitored closely.

wh.what: Bihar's only tiger reserve and national park
wh.where: Pashchim Champaran, on the Nepal border
wh.why: Contiguous habitat with Chitwan National Park

questions.status: Tiger numbers are small but stable, and camera traps record movement from Nepal.
why_wrong: Gaya has Bodh Gaya and the Barabar caves, not a tiger reserve.
Nalanda is an archaeological landscape.
Kaimur has hills and rock art but no tiger reserve.
questions.tip: One national park in Bihar — Valmiki. Any other name is a distractor.
questions.improve: Learn the Terai Arc Landscape reserves across Bihar, UP and Uttarakhand.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following Fundamental Rights are available only to citizens and not to foreigners?
1. Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination
2. Article 19 — six freedoms
3. Article 21 — protection of life and personal liberty
4. Article 29 — protection of interests of minorities
questions.history: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 use the word 'citizen', while Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 28 speak of 'persons'.
questions.discussion: The distinction is textual, not moral: the Constitution deliberately limits political and cultural rights to citizens while extending life, liberty, equality before law and religion to every person, including foreigners.

wh.why: Some rights attach to membership of the political community
wh.how: Read the subject clause of each article

questions.status: Article 21 has been expanded to include privacy, dignity, livelihood and a clean environment, and remains available to non-citizens.
why_wrong: Article 29 is also citizen-only, so this option is incomplete.
Article 21 is available to all persons, so this option is wrong.
Article 21 is not citizen-only.
questions.tip: Memorise the five citizen-only articles as a set: 15, 16, 19, 29, 30. Everything else in Part III covers persons.
questions.improve: Make a checklist of Part III articles marking citizen-only and person-based.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is:
questions.history: pH is the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration, and at 25°C pure water has equal concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻, each 10⁻⁷ mol per litre, giving pH 7.
questions.discussion: Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic. The scale is logarithmic, so a pH of 3 is a hundred times more acidic than pH 5, a point often missed in numerical questions.

wh.how: pH = -log[H⁺]
wh.why: It compresses a huge concentration range into a small scale

questions.status: pH is temperature dependent: neutral water shifts slightly below 7 at higher temperatures, though it stays neutral.
why_wrong: 0 is strongly acidic, as with concentrated hydrochloric acid.
14 is strongly basic, as with sodium hydroxide.
1 is strongly acidic.
questions.tip: Neutral equals 7 at 25°C only. Each unit step is a factor of ten, so use the logarithm before comparing.
questions.improve: Calculate pH for 0.01 M HCl and 0.01 M NaOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.history: Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of the atmosphere by volume, oxygen about 21 per cent, and argon just under 1 per cent.
questions.discussion: Carbon dioxide is present in only about 0.04 per cent, yet it matters disproportionately because of its greenhouse effect, which is why abundance and importance are separate questions.

wh.how: About 78 per cent by volume
wh.why: Nitrogen is relatively inert, so it accumulated rather than reacting away

questions.status: Atmospheric CO2 has risen from about 280 ppm in pre-industrial times to over 420 ppm today.
why_wrong: Oxygen is second at about 21 per cent.
CO2 is a trace gas at roughly 0.04 per cent.
Argon is a noble gas at just under 1 per cent.
questions.tip: Remember 78, 21, 1: nitrogen, oxygen, argon. Everything else is a trace gas.
questions.improve: Note the composition of the atmosphere and the share of greenhouse gases within it.
questions.source: NCERT Class IX Science, Natural Resources

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which letter is 5th to the right of the 10th letter from the left of the English alphabet?
questions.history: Alphabet position questions convert words into numbers, so the arithmetic is done on positions rather than letters.
questions.discussion: The 10th letter from the left is J. Moving 5 places right gives the 15th letter, which is O.

wh.how: Convert to numbers, add or subtract, convert back
wh.why: A fast scoring question in prelims

questions.status: Variants use the reverse alphabet, where A counts as 26.
why_wrong: N is the 14th letter, one place short.
P is the 16th letter, one place beyond.
M is the 13th letter, two places short.
questions.tip: Learn the landmark positions: E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25. They let you answer without reciting the alphabet.
questions.improve: Memorise EJOTY and CFILORUX as your two alphabet anchors.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: A price is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The net change is:
questions.history: Successive percentage changes multiply rather than add, so 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, a net fall of 4 per cent.
questions.discussion: The fall happens because the 20 per cent decrease is applied to a larger base than the original price, which is why the two changes do not cancel.

wh.what: Net effect of successive percentage changes
wh.how: a + b + ab/100, with signs
wh.why: Common in discount and profit questions

questions.status: Mains papers combine this with successive discounts in profit and loss.
why_wrong: No change is the intuitive but wrong answer.
4% increase would require a different order of magnitudes.
2% decrease comes from subtracting 20 and 18 instead of multiplying.
questions.tip: Use the formula a + b + ab/100 with signs: 20 + (-20) + (20 × -20)/100 = -4.
questions.improve: Test the formula with three successive changes to see how the error compounds.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'She has been working here ____ 2015.'
questions.history: Since marks a point in time from which an action continues, while for marks a duration.
questions.discussion: The present perfect continuous tense pairs with since plus a point in time, so 'since 2015' is correct, whereas 'for five years' would also be correct.

wh.how: Since for a point, for a duration
wh.why: A frequent fill-in-the-blank pattern

questions.status: Banking papers test since and for inside paragraphs rather than single sentences.
why_wrong: 'For' needs a duration such as five years.
'From' needs a matching 'to' in a range.
'In' with a year means during that year, not from then onwards.
questions.tip: Since takes a date or event, for takes a length of time. If the blank is followed by a year alone, it is since.
questions.improve: Write ten sentences using since and for correctly.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for dyarchy at the Centre.
2. It abolished dyarchy in the provinces.
3. It established the Reserve Bank of India.
questions.history: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy, ending the 1919 system of dyarchy in the provinces, and provided for dyarchy at the Centre — a provision that never came into force.
questions.discussion: The Act also created a Federal Court, a Federal Public Service Commission and a bicameral legislature in six provinces. The Reserve Bank was constituted under the separate Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, so statement 3 is wrong.

wh.why: To widen Indian participation while retaining British control at the centre

questions.status: The Act became the working constitution of British India until 1950 and shaped many provisions of the Indian Constitution.
why_wrong: Statement 3 is wrong: the RBI was created by the 1934 Act.
Statement 3 is wrong.
Statement 3 is wrong.
questions.tip: Separate Acts by year: RBI 1934, Government of India 1935, Federal Court 1937. One year per institution prevents this trap.
questions.improve: List the features of the 1919 and 1935 Acts side by side.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII, Modern India; Government of India Act 1935

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was launched against which system?
questions.history: Under tinkathia, tenants had to grow indigo on three kathas out of every twenty, and Gandhi's inquiry in Champaran forced the appointment of the Anderson Committee and abolition of the system.
questions.discussion: Champaran was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India and established his method: fact-finding, negotiation, then courting arrest to force a settlement.

wh.what: Peasant agitation against forced indigo cultivation
wh.who: Gandhi with Rajendra Prasad, Mazharul Haq and local planters
wh.why: Indigo prices had collapsed after synthetic dyes, so planters squeezed tenants

questions.status: Commemorated at the Gandhi Sangrahalaya in Motihari; the Champaran centenary was observed in 2017.
why_wrong: Zamindari revenue was the issue in Bengal's Permanent Settlement disputes.
Salt tax was the target of the 1930 Dandi March.
Begar was addressed later in Kheda and in the 1919 Punjab wrongs.
questions.tip: Gandhi's Indian movements in order: Champaran 1917, Ahmedabad mill 1918, Kheda 1918, then the all-India phase.
questions.improve: Write one paragraph on how tinkathia worked, since questions often test the mechanism.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a factor of production?
questions.history: Classical economics recognises four factors: land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship, with money serving only as a medium of exchange.
questions.discussion: Money buys capital but is not itself productive; capital means produced means of production such as machines and tools. This distinction is a favourite exam trap.

wh.why: Each factor earns a distinct reward: rent, wages, interest, profit

questions.status: Modern growth theory adds technology and human capital as separate contributors.
why_wrong: Land earns rent and is a primary factor.
Labour earns wages and is a primary factor.
Entrepreneurship organises the other factors and earns profit.
questions.tip: Money is a medium, capital is a machine. If you can touch and use it to produce, it is capital.
questions.improve: Match each factor to its reward and to one Indian example.

questions.subject: Political Science
questions.q: In political theory, sovereignty means:
options: Supreme and final authority within a territory
Rule by consent of the majority
questions.history: Sovereignty, elaborated by Bodin and later Austin, denotes the supreme and final law-making authority within a defined territory.
questions.discussion: Internal sovereignty concerns authority over citizens, while external sovereignty concerns independence from other States, and the two are often tested together.

wh.why: It distinguishes the State from other associations

questions.status: Globalisation and international institutions have qualified external sovereignty, a live debate in international relations.
why_wrong: Separation of powers is a structural principle, not sovereignty.
Majority rule describes a decision rule, not supreme authority.
Division of authority describes federalism.
questions.tip: Sovereignty is about who has the final word. Federalism is about who has which word.
questions.improve: Learn the four elements of the State: population, territory, government, sovereignty.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Political Science, Political Theory

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Montreal Protocol, aimed at protecting the ozone layer, was signed in which year?
questions.history: The Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987 to phase out chlorofluorocarbons, following the 1985 Vienna Convention and the discovery of the Antarctic ozone hole.
questions.discussion: The Kigali Amendment of 2016 extended the protocol to hydrofluorocarbons, which are not ozone depleting but are potent greenhouse gases.

wh.what: Treaty to phase out ozone depleting substances
wh.why: CFCs were thinning the stratospheric ozone layer
wh.how: Country-wise phase-out schedules with a multilateral fund

questions.status: India phased out HCFC-141b and is implementing the HFC phase-down under the India Cooling Action Plan.
why_wrong: 1985 is the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer, a framework without binding cuts.
1992 is the Rio Earth Summit and UNFCCC.
1997 is the Kyoto Protocol.
questions.tip: Ozone sequence: Vienna 1985, Montreal 1987, Kigali 2016.
questions.improve: Distinguish the ozone regime from the climate regime, UNFCCC 1992, Kyoto 1997, Paris 2015.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of force is:
questions.history: The newton is defined as the force that gives a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared.
questions.discussion: Units named after scientists follow the same pattern: force in newtons, energy in joules, power in watts, pressure in pascals. Each is a derived unit from the seven base units.

wh.how: F = ma, so kg m s⁻²
wh.why: Derived units must be traceable to base units

questions.status: The SI system was revised in 2019 so that all base units rest on defined constants rather than physical artefacts.
why_wrong: Joule is the unit of energy or work.
Watt is the unit of power.
Pascal is the unit of pressure.
questions.tip: Learn each derived unit by its formula: force ma, work Fd, power Fd/t, pressure F/A.
questions.improve: Write the seven SI base units and derive three units of your choice from them.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced in 1793 by which Governor-General?
questions.history: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793, fixing land revenue in perpetuity with zamindars as the revenue collectors.
questions.discussion: The settlement guaranteed State revenue and created a loyal rentier class, but it also entrenched absentee landlordism and left cultivators without security of tenure.

wh.what: A permanent land revenue system with zamindars
wh.why: To stabilise revenue and create allies for the Company

questions.status: Subsequently moderated by tenancy reforms and abolished formally in independent India by zamindari abolition laws.
why_wrong: Warren Hastings introduced the annual and five-yearly revenue experiments before 1793.
Wellesley built the subsidiary alliance system.
Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.
questions.tip: Pair the three settlements: Permanent (Bengal, Cornwallis), Ryotwari (Madras/Bombay, Munro), Mahalwari (North India, Holt Mackenzie).
questions.improve: Write one line on who lost land under each settlement; that framing answers most questions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which river is popularly called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.history: The Kosi shifts its course by up to 150 km across north Bihar, and its floods since the 1950s have earned it the name Sorrow of Bihar.
questions.discussion: Heavy silt load from the Nepal hills raises the river bed, so embankments fail and the river avulses into new channels, a textbook case of a shifting braided stream.

wh.what: A north Bihar Himalayan river prone to avulsion
wh.where: Flows from Nepal into the Ganga near Kursela
wh.why: Extremely high silt load and low gradient on the plains
wh.how: Embankments and spurs have contained but not solved flooding

questions.status: The Kosi high dam proposal in Nepal remains unresolved; Bihar continues structural and non-structural flood measures.
why_wrong: The Gandak floods but is not the traditional Sorrow of Bihar.
The Son is a southern tributary and not a flood scourge.
The Ghaghara floods eastern UP more than Bihar.
questions.tip: Two sorrows to keep apart: Kosi for Bihar, Damodar for Bengal (also called the Sorrow of Bengal).
questions.improve: Map the eight north Bihar rivers and their Nepal origins in one diagram.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.history: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave and needs a material medium to propagate, which is why space is silent.
questions.discussion: Speed varies with medium elasticity and density: fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases. That is why a train is heard through the rails before it is heard through the air.

wh.why: Particles must vibrate and transfer energy
wh.how: Compressions and rarefactions travel through the medium

questions.status: Spacecraft communications use radio waves, which are electromagnetic and need no medium.
why_wrong: Solids transmit sound fastest.
Liquids transmit sound well, as whales demonstrate.
Gases transmit sound, though more slowly.
questions.tip: Mechanical waves need a medium, electromagnetic waves do not. Sound is mechanical, light is electromagnetic.
questions.improve: Learn the approximate speed of sound in air, water and steel.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: The accounting equation is best expressed as:
questions.history: The equation follows from double entry: everything a business owns was financed either by outsiders (liabilities) or by owners (capital).
questions.discussion: Every transaction keeps the equation balanced, which is why the balance sheet always ties. If assets rise without a matching liability, capital must rise too, as with cash brought in by the owner.

wh.how: Every transaction affects at least two elements equally
wh.why: It is the basis of the balance sheet

questions.status: Under Ind AS and IFRS the same identity holds, though presentation and measurement rules have changed.
why_wrong: Subtracting capital would make the equation collapse for any profitable business.
Capital is a residual claim, not the sum of assets and liabilities.
This reverses the owner and outsider claims.
questions.tip: Read it as a sentence: what the business owns equals what it owes to outsiders plus what it owes to owners.
questions.improve: Take ten transactions and show the effect of each on all three elements.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Opportunity cost refers to:
options: The money paid for a good
The value of the next best alternative forgone
The cost of producing one more unit
The total cost of all alternatives
questions.history: Opportunity cost is central to the definition of economics as the study of allocating scarce resources among competing ends.
questions.discussion: It explains why a free good can still have a cost: choosing to study for an exam has the opportunity cost of the earnings forgone. It differs from accounting cost, which records only actual payments.

wh.why: Resources are scarce and uses compete
wh.how: Identify the next best option you gave up

questions.status: Used in project appraisal and policy analysis under the term shadow price.
why_wrong: Money paid is accounting cost, not opportunity cost.
That is marginal cost.
Opportunity cost counts one forgone alternative, not all of them.
questions.tip: Whenever a question asks what you gave up, the answer is opportunity cost.
questions.improve: Apply opportunity cost to a real decision you made this month.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Elements of group 18 of the modern periodic table are called:
questions.history: Group 18 holds helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon, whose filled outer shells make them chemically inert in most conditions.
questions.discussion: Their very high ionisation energies explain why they form almost no compounds; xenon fluorides were the first exceptions, and those required extreme conditions.

wh.why: Complete valence shells mean no tendency to gain or lose electrons

questions.status: Used in lighting, welding shields, MRI magnets with liquid helium, and inert atmospheres.
why_wrong: Alkali metals are group 1.
Halogens are group 17.
Transition metals are groups 3 to 12.
questions.tip: Groups at a glance: 1 alkali, 2 alkaline earth, 17 halogens, 18 noble gases.
questions.improve: Learn the group names and one property of each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Chemistry, Classification of Elements

questions.subject: Computer Fundamentals
questions.q: The decimal number 10 in binary is:
questions.history: Decimal to binary conversion repeatedly divides by two and reads the remainders upward, giving 1010 for ten.
questions.discussion: Verify by expanding: 1×8 + 0×4 + 1×2 + 0×1 = 10. That check catches nearly every conversion mistake under exam pressure.

wh.how: Divide by 2, record remainders, read bottom to top
wh.why: Computers represent values in binary states

questions.status: Hexadecimal is used as shorthand for binary in memory dumps and colour codes.
why_wrong: 1100 is 12 in decimal.
1001 is 9 in decimal.
1110 is 14 in decimal.
questions.tip: Place values from the right are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Add the ones that are switched on and you have the decimal value.
questions.improve: Convert 25, 37 and 100 into binary and back.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Find the error: 'He do not like tea.'
questions.history: In the simple present tense, third-person singular subjects take 'does', not 'do'.
questions.discussion: The corrected sentence is 'He does not like tea'. Spotting the subject-verb agreement is the single most common error type in these papers.

wh.how: Match the auxiliary to the subject's person and number
wh.why: Grammar accuracy is a high-yield area

questions.status: Modern exams embed errors in longer sentences to slow the reader down.
why_wrong: 'He' is correct as the subject.
'Not' correctly negates the auxiliary.
'Like' is the correct base form after 'does not'.
questions.tip: For error spotting, check three things first: subject-verb agreement, tense consistency and preposition use.
questions.improve: Do ten agreement exercises covering collective nouns and indefinite pronouns.

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Purchase of machinery for ₹5,00,000 is an example of:
questions.history: Capital expenditure creates or enhances a long-term asset and appears in the balance sheet, while revenue expenditure is consumed within the period.
questions.discussion: The test is benefit period, not amount. A ₹5,000 printer used for five years is capital, while a ₹5,00,000 salary bill is revenue.

wh.how: Ask whether the benefit extends beyond one accounting year
wh.why: Misclassification distorts profit and the balance sheet

questions.status: Ind AS 16 requires capitalisation of directly attributable costs, including installation and testing.
why_wrong: Revenue expenditure is consumed in the current period, such as wages.
Deferred revenue expenditure is a legacy Indian concept, largely subsumed under Ind AS.
A contingent liability is a possible obligation, not a payment made.
questions.tip: Amount does not decide. Duration of benefit decides. That one line settles most classification questions.
questions.improve: List ten common expenditures and classify each with one line of reasoning.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Accountancy; Ind AS 16

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
questions.history: In analogy questions the relationship must be identical on both sides: a professional to the place of work.
questions.discussion: A doctor works in a hospital as a teacher works in a school; student, book and class are related but describe different relationships.

wh.how: State the relationship in words before choosing
wh.why: Tests precise relationship mapping

questions.status: Higher-level papers use tool-to-user or cause-to-effect analogies.
why_wrong: Student is the recipient of teaching, not the workplace.
Book is a tool, not a place.
Class is a group or a session, not the institution.
questions.tip: Say the relationship aloud as a sentence; if it does not read naturally with the option, reject it.
questions.improve: Build a list of ten relationship types with one example each.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which amendment, and on whose recommendation?
questions.history: Part IVA, Article 51A, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, listing ten duties.
questions.discussion: The 86th Amendment later added an eleventh duty on education of children aged 6-14. Duties remain non-justiciable but are cited by courts while interpreting reasonableness of restrictions.

wh.why: The Emergency-era state wanted civic obligation alongside rights

questions.status: Not enforceable directly; Parliament may enact laws to enforce them, as with the flag code and environmental statutes.
why_wrong: The 44th Amendment restored civil liberties after the Emergency and reduced the amending power's reach.
The 52nd Amendment dealt with anti-defection.
The 73rd Amendment created Panchayati Raj institutions.
questions.tip: Group the 42nd Amendment's four big moves: Preamble words, Fundamental Duties, mini-constitution changes to the judiciary, and transfer of education to the concurrent list.
questions.improve: Learn all eleven duties in a single sentence each so elimination questions become easy.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: What is the State animal of Bihar?
questions.history: Bihar declared the gaur as its State animal, with the house sparrow as State bird, peepal as State tree and marigold as State flower.
questions.discussion: The gaur is the largest extant wild bovine, and its association with Bihar is largely symbolic since wild populations sit in the Valmiki landscape.

wh.where: Valmiki Tiger Reserve holds the State's main large mammal populations

questions.status: Gaur is listed as Vulnerable by IUCN, with the largest populations in the Western Ghats.
why_wrong: The tiger is India's national animal and Bihar's flagship in Valmiki, but not the State animal.
The elephant is the State animal of Kerala and Jharkhand.
The leopard is not a State symbol anywhere in this region.
questions.tip: State symbols of Bihar: gaur, house sparrow, peepal, marigold. Memorise as one four-item set.
questions.improve: Learn state symbols for Bihar, UP, Jharkhand and West Bengal together to avoid swaps.
questions.source: Government of Bihar notifications; IUCN Red List

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: Find the simple interest on ₹8,000 at 7.5% per annum for 2 years.
questions.history: Simple interest is calculated as principal × rate × time divided by 100, without any compounding on accrued interest.
questions.discussion: The trap in this question is reading 7.5% as 7% or 8%; keeping the decimal intact gives 8000 × 7.5 × 2 / 100 = 1200.

wh.how: SI = P × R × T / 100
wh.why: Used for short-term loans and some recurring deposits

questions.status: In exams, simple interest questions are usually combined with part-payment or instalment problems.
why_wrong: ₹1,100 comes from rounding the rate to 7% for 2 years.
₹1,250 would need a rate near 7.8%.
₹1,400 comes from treating the rate as 8.75%.
questions.tip: For 2 years, SI is just 2 × P × R / 100. Compute one year's interest first, then double it.
questions.improve: Practise five part-payment SI problems, which are the harder variant.

questions.subject: GST
questions.q: For an intra-State supply of goods, which taxes are levied?
questions.history: Intra-State supplies attract Central GST and State GST equally, while inter-State supplies attract Integrated GST, which is then apportioned between the Centre and the destination State.
questions.discussion: The design makes the tax destination based: revenue accrues to the State where the goods are consumed, not where they are produced.

wh.how: CGST plus SGST at half the notified rate each
wh.why: To preserve fiscal autonomy of States within one market

questions.status: Rate rationalisation into fewer slabs has been discussed repeatedly by the GST Council.
why_wrong: IGST applies to inter-State supply.
CGST never pairs with IGST on the same supply.
SGST alone would deny the Centre its share.
questions.tip: Inside the State means two taxes, CGST and SGST. Across States means one tax, IGST.
questions.improve: Compute the tax on a ₹10,000 intra-State and inter-State sale at 18 per cent.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon, known as the Dhammachakka-pravartana?
questions.history: After enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, the Buddha preached the first sermon at the Deer Park in Sarnath, near Varanasi, setting the wheel of law in motion.
questions.discussion: The four sites of the Buddha's life story map neatly onto four events: birth at Lumbini, enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, first sermon at Sarnath, and mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar.

wh.what: First sermon and the Four Noble Truths
wh.who: Gautama Buddha to his five former companions
wh.why: To set out the middle path and the eightfold path

questions.status: Sarnath remains an archaeological and pilgrimage site with the Dhamek Stupa marking the event.
why_wrong: Bodh Gaya is the place of enlightenment under the Bodhi tree.
Kushinagar is where the Buddha passed away.
Rajgriha hosted the first Buddhist council after his death.
questions.tip: Attach every event to one site and one council; Buddhist councils are a recurring question set.
questions.improve: Learn the four Buddhist councils with venue, patron and outcome in a four-row table.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History

questions.subject: Computer Fundamentals
questions.q: Which of the following is a volatile memory?
questions.history: RAM loses its contents when power is removed, which is why unsaved work disappears in a power cut, while ROM retains data permanently.
questions.discussion: Volatility is about persistence without power, not about speed. RAM is both volatile and fast, while flash storage is non-volatile and slower.

wh.why: RAM needs constant refresh to hold charge
wh.how: DRAM uses capacitors that leak charge

questions.status: DRAM and SRAM remain volatile; emerging technologies such as MRAM aim to combine speed with persistence.
why_wrong: ROM is non-volatile and retains data without power.
A hard disk is non-volatile magnetic storage.
A flash drive is non-volatile solid state storage.
questions.tip: If losing power would erase it, it is volatile. RAM is the only common example in exam options.
questions.improve: Compare RAM, ROM, cache and secondary storage on speed, volatility and cost per GB.

questions.subject: Taxation
questions.q: Under the old tax regime, the maximum deduction available under Section 80C is:
questions.history: Section 80C allows deduction up to ₹1,50,000 for specified investments and payments including PPF, ELSS, life insurance premia and principal repayment of housing loans.
questions.discussion: The limit is a ceiling for the aggregate of 80C and the linked 80CCC and 80CCD(1) provisions, which is why taxpayers often need to plan across instruments rather than one.

wh.where: Chapter VI-A of the Income Tax Act
wh.why: To encourage long-term savings

questions.status: The new regime under Section 115BAC, the default from 2023-24, does not allow the 80C deduction, so the choice of regime matters.
why_wrong: ₹1,00,000 was the limit before it was raised to ₹1,50,000.
₹2,00,000 is not an 80C limit.
₹2,50,000 applies to certain other provisions, not 80C.
questions.tip: Keep the three numbers apart: 80C ₹1.5 lakh, 80D health insurance, 24(b) home loan interest ₹2 lakh.
questions.improve: Compare the old and new regimes for a sample income of ₹12 lakh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian States?
questions.history: The Tropic of Cancer at 23°30' N crosses eight States: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
questions.discussion: The line is used in mapping questions because it neatly divides India into a northern temperate and a southern tropical zone, influencing cropping and monsoon behaviour.

wh.where: Eight States from Gujarat to Mizoram
wh.why: It separates tropical from subtropical climate zones
wh.how: Passes near Bhopal, Ranchi and Agartala

questions.status: A standard prelims fact, frequently combined with questions on the Standard Meridian at 82°30' E.
why_wrong: Six undercounts the line, which also crosses Jharkhand and Tripura.
Seven drops Mizoram, the last State before Myanmar.
Nine is a common overcount; no ninth State touches the line.
questions.tip: Recite the eight in west-to-east order as a chant; add Bihar and Odisha deliberately as the two distractors that do not belong.
questions.improve: Draw India's outline once and mark the Tropic of Cancer and Standard Meridian from memory.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Which district of Bihar is the largest by area?
questions.history: Pashchim Champaran, in the north-west along the Nepal border, is the largest district by area at roughly 5,229 square kilometres.
questions.discussion: Patna is the largest by population but small in area, which is why the two superlatives are usually tested together.

wh.why: Its forest and Terai belt extends over a wide tract

questions.status: It contains the Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar's only national park area.
why_wrong: Patna is the most populous district but ranks low on area.
Muzaffarpur is a populous north Bihar district but smaller in area.
Bhagalpur is a medium-sized district on the Ganga.
questions.tip: Largest by area is Pashchim Champaran; largest by population is Patna. Learn them as a pair.
questions.improve: Note the three smallest and three largest districts of Bihar by area.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 5 : 6, then A : B : C equals:
questions.history: When a common term appears in two ratios, it is made equal by taking the LCM of its values before combining.
questions.discussion: Here B is 4 in the first ratio and 5 in the second, so both ratios are scaled by the other's B value, giving 15:20 and 20:24.

wh.how: Equalise the common term, then merge
wh.why: Ratio chaining is a base skill for partnership and mixture problems

questions.status: Frequently combined with partnership profit-sharing in mains-level papers.
why_wrong: 3:4:6 ignores the mismatch in B's value between the two ratios.
5:4:6 reverses the ratios instead of combining them.
3:5:6 drops B's actual scaling entirely.
questions.tip: Write the two ratios one above the other, align the common term, and cross-multiply. It never fails.
questions.improve: Do five three-ratio combination sums until the alignment becomes automatic.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Bihar shares its state boundaries with how many Indian States?
questions.history: Bihar borders Uttar Pradesh to the west, Jharkhand to the south and West Bengal to the east, while Nepal lies along its northern international boundary.
questions.discussion: The 2011 census counted 38 districts in Bihar; the State is landlocked and drained by the Ganga and its northern tributaries.

wh.where: Eastern India, on the Nepal border
wh.why: A common map-based question
wh.how: UP, Jharkhand, West Bengal

questions.status: Bihar has no coastline and is one of India's most densely populated States.
why_wrong: Two undercounts; Jharkhand and West Bengal are easy to forget.
Four would require an additional State such as Odisha, which does not touch Bihar.
Five is well beyond the actual count.
questions.tip: Three States and one country — that single sentence prevents most errors here.
questions.improve: Draw Bihar and label its three neighbours plus the districts along the Nepal border.
questions.source: Census of India 2011; Survey of India

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: The Sonepur cattle fair is held at the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.history: Sonepur in Saran district hosts Asia's largest cattle fair at the meeting point of the Ganga and the Gandak, traditionally beginning on Kartik Purnima.
questions.discussion: The fair's religious anchor is the Harihar Nath temple, and its trade character has shifted from elephants and cattle to horses, and now mostly to local livestock and cultural events.

wh.why: River confluence pilgrimage plus livestock trade

questions.status: The elephant trade ended after 2003 restrictions; the fair now emphasises rural tourism.
why_wrong: The Son meets the Ganga further east near Patna, not at Sonepur.
The Kosi joins the Ganga near Kursela, far downstream.
The Punpun is a small southern tributary of the Ganga.
questions.tip: Two confluences to keep apart: Sonepur is Ganga-Gandak, Patna's confluence area is Ganga-Son.
questions.improve: Mark Bihar's main rivers and their confluences on an outline map.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In photosynthesis, oxygen is released from the splitting of:
questions.history: Photosystem II splits water through photolysis to replace the electrons it loses, releasing oxygen as a by-product.
questions.discussion: This was established using isotope labelling with oxygen-18, which showed the released gas came from water rather than carbon dioxide, settling a long-standing debate.

wh.how: Photolysis of water in photosystem II
wh.why: To replenish electrons lost by chlorophyll

questions.status: Artificial photosynthesis research aims to replicate water splitting for hydrogen fuel.
why_wrong: Carbon dioxide is reduced to carbohydrate and its oxygen ends up in glucose and water.
Glucose is a product, not a source.
Chlorophyll is the pigment that absorbs light, not a substrate.
questions.tip: The isotope experiment is the evidence; remember that the answer is water, not carbon dioxide.
questions.improve: Write the overall photosynthesis equation and label the light and dark reactions.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Biology, Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the highest mountain peak located entirely within Indian territory?
questions.history: Kangchenjunga at 8,586 m on the Sikkim-Nepal border is the highest peak wholly within Indian territory; K2 at 8,611 m lies in territory claimed by India but administered by Pakistan.
questions.discussion: The wording matters in exams. 'Highest in India' has been contested since 1959, while 'highest entirely within India' is settled at Kangchenjunga.

wh.what: 8,586 m peak in the eastern Himalayas
wh.when: First climbed in 1955 by a British expedition
wh.why: It marks the eastern anchor of the high Himalayan wall

questions.status: Kangchenjunga is a protected biosphere and a restricted-access climbing zone with a tradition of stopping short of the summit out of religious respect.
why_wrong: K2 lies in Pakistan-administered territory, though India claims the region.
Nanda Devi at 7,816 m is the highest peak entirely within India after Kangchenjunga.
Nanga Parbat is in Pakistan-administered territory.
questions.tip: Read the qualifier before the options: 'entirely within' changes the answer from K2 to Kangchenjunga.
questions.improve: List the top ten Indian peaks with State and height; note which are on borders.
questions.source: Survey of India; NCERT Class XI

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Tenth Schedule, dealing with anti-defection, was inserted by which amendment?
questions.history: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 added the Tenth Schedule to curb the culture of defection that toppled governments through the 1960s and 1970s.
questions.discussion: The 91st Amendment later removed the one-third split exemption, so only a merger of two-thirds of a legislature party is protected. The Speaker decides disqualification, a role the Supreme Court has repeatedly asked to be time-bound.

wh.why: Political instability from floor-crossing

questions.status: Decisional delays by Speakers remain the core criticism; courts have set outer timelines in recent cases.
why_wrong: The 42nd Amendment dealt with the mini-constitution changes.
The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18.
The 91st Amendment limited the Council of Ministers size and removed the split exemption.
questions.tip: Link schedules to numbers: First = States and UTs, Seventh = three lists, Eighth = languages, Ninth = land reform laws, Tenth = defection, Eleventh = Panchayats, Twelfth = Municipalities.
questions.improve: Note three Supreme Court decisions on Speaker delay and the relief granted in each.
questions.source: Constitution of India, Tenth Schedule; 52nd and 91st Amendments

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: A train 180 m long running at 54 km/h crosses a pole in how many seconds?
questions.history: To cross a pole, a train covers exactly its own length, so time equals length divided by speed.
questions.discussion: The only step that trips candidates is the unit change: 54 km/h multiplied by 5/18 gives 15 m/s, and 180 divided by 15 is 12 seconds.

wh.what: Time to cross a stationary point
wh.how: Time = length / speed
wh.why: A recurring SSC and railway question type

questions.status: Variants ask for a platform, where the length of the platform is added to the train's length.
why_wrong: 10 seconds assumes a speed of 18 m/s.
14 seconds comes from rounding 12.86 after a unit error.
15 seconds confuses the km/h figure with m/s.
questions.tip: Multiply km/h by 5/18 to get m/s instantly. For a pole use train length, for a platform add both lengths.
questions.improve: Solve three platform-crossing and two overtaking problems in the same sitting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Insulin, which regulates blood glucose, is secreted by which organ?
questions.history: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin, while alpha cells secrete glucagon, and the two together regulate blood glucose.
questions.discussion: The liver is the target rather than the source: insulin signals it to store glucose as glycogen, which is why liver function and insulin action are usually studied together.

wh.why: To move glucose from blood into cells

questions.status: Recombinant human insulin, produced since 1982, replaced animal-derived insulin in diabetes treatment.
why_wrong: The liver stores glycogen but does not secrete insulin.
The kidney filters blood and produces erythropoietin.
The thyroid secretes thyroxine, which regulates metabolism.
questions.tip: Pancreas is both exocrine and endocrine. Insulin and glucagon come from its endocrine part, the islets.
questions.improve: Learn the major endocrine glands and one hormone each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chemical Coordination and Integration

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of Bihar?
questions.history: Rabri Devi became Bihar's first woman Chief Minister in July 1997 and held the post across three separate terms until 2005.
questions.discussion: Her entry followed Lalu Prasad's resignation after a chargesheet in the fodder scam, making her tenure a frequently tested fact in state politics questions.

wh.what: First woman Chief Minister of Bihar

questions.status: She later served as Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Council.
why_wrong: Sushila Keto is an activist, not a Chief Minister.
Meira Kumar was a Union Minister and the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Sushma Swaraj was Chief Minister of Delhi briefly and a Union Minister.
questions.tip: First woman CM facts: Bihar Rabri Devi, Delhi Sushma Swaraj, Tamil Nadu Jayalalithaa, UP Sucheta Kripalani.
questions.improve: Keep a small table of firsts in Indian politics by State.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI consists of how many members?
questions.history: The six-member MPC was constituted in 2016 under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act: three from the RBI including the Governor, and three appointed by the Central Government.
questions.discussion: The Governor has a casting vote in a tie, and the committee must meet at least four times a year, though it meets bi-monthly in practice.

wh.what: Body that sets the policy repo rate
wh.who: Governor, Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer, three government nominees
wh.why: To bring transparency and accountability to rate setting

questions.status: The inflation targeting framework is due for review; the 4 per cent target with a 2 to 6 per cent band has been retained so far.
why_wrong: Four is too small and does not match the statutory composition.
Five would create a permanent tie risk.
Eight would give the government an outright majority.
questions.tip: Six members, three plus three, Governor breaks ties — three facts answer most MPC questions.
questions.improve: Learn the MPC's statutory duties and the escape clause for missing the inflation target.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: At what rate of simple interest will a sum double itself in 8 years?
questions.history: Doubling means the interest equals the principal, so 100 = 100 × R × 8 / 100, giving R = 12.5 per cent.
questions.discussion: A useful shortcut for doubling questions is R × T = 100. Here 100/8 gives 12.5 immediately.

wh.what: Rate needed to double a sum
wh.how: R × T = 100 for doubling under SI
wh.why: A recurring one-line question

questions.status: For tripling under simple interest, the product R × T equals 200.
why_wrong: 10% would double in 10 years.
15% would double in about 6.7 years.
8% would double in 12.5 years.
questions.tip: Doubling under SI: R × T = 100. Tripling: R × T = 200. Quadrupling: R × T = 300.
questions.improve: Convert the same question to compound interest, where the rule of 72 applies instead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The double helix structure of DNA was proposed by:
questions.history: James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix model in 1953, drawing critically on the X-ray diffraction work of Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.
questions.discussion: The model explained base pairing and replication, and Franklin's Photograph 51 was the evidence that made the helical geometry unavoidable.

wh.who: Watson and Crick, with Franklin's diffraction data
wh.why: To explain how genetic information is stored and copied

questions.status: Franklin's contribution is now widely acknowledged; the Nobel Prize in 1962 went only to Watson, Crick and Wilkins.
why_wrong: Mendel established the laws of inheritance without knowing about DNA.
Darwin proposed natural selection.
Hooke coined the term cell after observing cork.
questions.tip: Keep the roles apart: Mendel for inheritance laws, Watson and Crick for structure, Franklin for the diffraction evidence.
questions.improve: Learn the four base pairs and the difference between DNA and RNA.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Biology, Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Which error will NOT be disclosed by a trial balance?
options: Wrong totalling of a subsidiary book
Posting only the debit side of a transaction
An error of principle, such as machinery purchase debited to Purchases
A casting error while totalling the trial balance
questions.history: A trial balance tests arithmetical accuracy only, so errors that keep debits and credits equal pass through undetected; an error of principle is one such case.
questions.discussion: Compensating errors can also escape detection, but a principle error is the textbook case: the books balance, yet the profit and the balance sheet are both wrong.

wh.how: Check whether debits and credits stay equal
wh.why: Examiners test the concept, not just the format

questions.status: Modern curricula teach this alongside the suspense account treatment for one-sided errors.
why_wrong: Wrong totalling usually creates an unequal trial balance.
One-sided posting always creates a difference.
A casting error in the trial balance itself is precisely what re-totalling detects.
questions.tip: A trial balance catches arithmetic, not judgement. Anything that touches the nature of the account escapes it.
questions.improve: List the four types of errors that a trial balance cannot detect with one example each.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A person facing north turns 90° clockwise, then 180°. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.history: Direction sense questions track orientation changes rather than physical movement.
questions.discussion: From north, 90° clockwise brings him east; a further 180° reverses that to west. Adding the turns first, 270° clockwise from north, also gives west.

wh.how: Add the angles, then convert to a compass direction
wh.why: Tests spatial reasoning under time pressure

questions.status: Exam variants include multiple turns plus walking distances.
why_wrong: North would need a full 360° of turning.
South would be a single 180° turn from north.
East is the position after only the first turn.
questions.tip: Draw a small compass and rotate your pen, not your mind. Add all turns first, then read the final direction once.
questions.improve: Solve five direction questions that also ask for final distance using Pythagoras.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The largest organ of the human body is:
questions.history: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight, forming the integumentary system that covers roughly two square metres in an adult.
questions.discussion: The liver is the largest internal organ and the largest gland, which is why both statements are true and examiners exploit the difference in wording.

wh.why: It covers the entire body and performs barrier, sensory and thermal functions
wh.how: Three layers: epidermis, dermis and hypodermis

questions.status: Skin is also a major route for drug delivery and a site for vitamin D synthesis.
why_wrong: The liver is the largest internal organ and gland, but not the largest organ overall.
The brain is large but far lighter than the skin.
Lungs are paired organs and smaller by mass.
questions.tip: Read the wording: largest organ is skin, largest internal organ is liver, largest gland is liver.
questions.improve: Learn the three layers of skin and one function of each.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Biology, Structural Organisation in Animals

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The photoelectric effect provided evidence that light behaves as:
options: A stream of particles called photons
questions.history: Einstein explained the photoelectric effect in 1905 by proposing that light arrives in discrete quanta of energy hf, later called photons.
questions.discussion: The decisive observation was that below a threshold frequency no electrons are emitted however intense the light, which wave theory cannot explain but photon theory predicts exactly.

wh.why: Classical wave theory could not explain the threshold frequency

questions.status: Photoelectric detectors now underpin solar cells, night-vision tubes and photomultiplier sensors.
why_wrong: Wave behaviour explains interference but not the threshold frequency.
Magnetic fields are unrelated to the emission threshold.
Light is transverse, not longitudinal, and that is separate from the quantum issue.
questions.tip: Interference proves light is a wave, photoelectric effect proves it is a particle. Both are true, which is wave-particle duality.
questions.improve: Write Einstein's photoelectric equation and explain each term.
questions.source: NCERT Class XII Physics, Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy were inspired mainly by the Constitution of which country?
questions.history: Part IV of the Constitution drew on the Irish Constitution of 1937, which itself had carried forward the Spanish and papal social encyclical tradition.
questions.discussion: The Irish link explains the unusual mix of welfare socialism and Gandhian village industry in Part IV. The US gave us fundamental rights, Ireland gave us the aspirations.

wh.why: To balance individual liberty with social justice
wh.how: Articles 36 to 51 of Part IV

questions.status: Courts increasingly read DPSP together with fundamental rights, as in the right to health and clean environment.
why_wrong: The US contributed fundamental rights and judicial review, not the Directive Principles.
Australia gave the idea of concurrent lists and freedom of trade.
Canada inspired the federation with a strong centre and residuary powers.
questions.tip: Fix one borrowing per country: Ireland DPSP, US FR and judicial review, UK parliamentary system, Canada strong centre, Australia concurrent list, USSR fundamental duties.
questions.improve: Write down three DPSP that have become enforceable rights through judgments.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's monetary policy framework, consider the following statements:
1. An increase in the cash reserve ratio reduces the lendable resources of banks.
2. The marginal standing facility rate is normally above the repo rate.
3. The liquidity corridor is bounded by the marginal standing facility rate and the standing deposit facility rate.
questions.history: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility corridor has the MSF as its ceiling and, since 2022, the Standing Deposit Facility as its floor, with the repo rate inside the corridor.
questions.discussion: CRR is a cash reserve held with the RBI and earns no interest, so raising it directly shrinks lendable funds. The MSF sits 25 basis points above the repo, allowing banks to borrow against securities in an emergency. The SDF floor lets the RBI absorb liquidity without collateral.

wh.who: RBI and the Monetary Policy Committee
wh.how: CRR, repo, SDF floor, MSF ceiling
wh.why: To keep the call money rate inside a target band

questions.status: The SDF replaced the fixed reverse repo as the operative floor in April 2022.
why_wrong: Statement 3 is also correct, so this is incomplete.
Statement 1 is correct, so this is incomplete.
Statement 2 is correct, so this is incomplete.
questions.tip: Draw the corridor vertically: MSF on top, repo in the middle, SDF at the bottom. Every question about rates becomes a position on that line.
questions.improve: Learn which instrument is quantitative (CRR, SLR) and which is rate-based (repo, MSF, SDF).

questions.subject: DBMS
questions.q: In a relational database, a primary key must be:
questions.history: A primary key uniquely identifies each row, so the relational model requires both uniqueness and the absence of nulls, since a null cannot identify anything.
questions.discussion: A candidate key that is not chosen as primary becomes an alternate key, and a foreign key in another table references the primary key to enforce referential integrity.

wh.how: Unique constraint plus not null constraint
wh.why: Every row must be addressable and unambiguous

questions.status: Surrogate keys such as auto-increment ids are now common in place of natural keys.
why_wrong: A nullable unique column is a unique key, not a primary key.
Duplicates defeat the purpose of identification.
Every row must carry a primary key value.
questions.tip: Primary key equals unique plus not null. Both conditions must appear in the option for it to be correct.
questions.improve: Write the SQL for creating a table with primary and foreign keys.
questions.source: BCA DBMS syllabus; Codd's relational model

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The repo rate is the rate at which:
options: Banks lend to their best customers
RBI lends short-term funds to banks against government securities
Banks lend to each other overnight
questions.history: Repo is a repurchase agreement: the RBI lends against government securities with an agreement to buy them back, making it the policy rate since the LAF was introduced in 2000.
questions.discussion: The reverse repo, now the Standing Deposit Facility, absorbs liquidity. The corridor between them steers the call money rate.

wh.what: RBI's short-term lending rate to banks
wh.why: It transmits policy to lending and deposit rates
wh.how: Through the Liquidity Adjustment Facility

questions.status: The SDF introduced in 2022 replaced the fixed reverse repo as the floor of the corridor.
why_wrong: That is the base rate or MCLR, set by each bank.
That describes the reverse repo or the Standing Deposit Facility.
That is the call money rate, determined by the market.
questions.tip: Repo means RBI gives money, reverse repo means RBI takes money. The direction is the whole answer.
questions.improve: Draw the liquidity corridor with SDF, repo and MSF, and label who borrows from whom.
questions.source: RBI Monetary Policy framework; NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The idiom 'to bite the bullet' means:
options: To endure a painful situation bravely
To take a risk without preparation
questions.history: The phrase is often traced to soldiers biting a lead bullet during surgery before anaesthesia existed, though the earliest written record is nineteenth-century.
questions.discussion: Idiom questions reward knowing the figurative sense, not the literal words; the literal reading is exactly what the distractors exploit.

wh.how: Learn idioms as whole phrases with one example sentence
wh.why: Idioms appear in every SSC and banking paper

questions.status: Exams favour idioms with military or nautical origins.
why_wrong: Speaking rudely describes 'to talk back' or 'to snap at someone'.
Taking an unprepared risk is 'to take a leap in the dark'.
Refusing to cooperate is 'to dig in one's heels'.
questions.tip: Store idioms with one sentence you invent yourself; the sentence is what you will recall in the exam.
questions.improve: Learn five idioms a day with a self-written sentence each.

questions.subject: Bihar Special
questions.q: Bihar was carved out as a separate province on which date, now celebrated as Bihar Diwas?
questions.history: On 22 March 1912 the British carved Bihar out of the Bengal Presidency, with Patna as its capital; the day has been observed as Bihar Diwas since 2010.
questions.discussion: The 1912 separation followed the 1905 partition of Bengal and a long campaign for a separate administrative identity, and it also created Orissa as a separate province in 1936.

wh.why: Administrative size and demands for separate identity

questions.status: Bihar Diwas is a state holiday with a three-day cultural programme at Gandhi Maidan, Patna.
why_wrong: 1 April 1912 relates to other administrative changes, not the creation of Bihar.
1947 is independence, not the province's formation.
1950 is when the Constitution came into force.
questions.tip: Fix 22 March 1912 as Bihar's birthday and remember it was separated from Bengal, not from UP.
questions.improve: Note the three separations of that period: Bihar 1912, Orissa 1936, and the annulled partition of Bengal 1905.
questions.source: Government of Bihar; Bihar Diwas records

questions.subject: GST
questions.q: The general threshold turnover for mandatory GST registration for suppliers of goods is:
questions.history: The threshold for goods was raised to ₹40 lakh for normal category States, while services remain at ₹20 lakh, with lower limits for special category States.
questions.discussion: Thresholds apply to aggregate turnover, which includes exempt supplies and exports, so a dealer cannot avoid registration by keeping taxable turnover low.

wh.why: Small dealers should not carry full compliance cost
wh.how: Aggregate turnover across all registrations under one PAN

questions.status: Composition scheme thresholds are separate and lower for services.
why_wrong: ₹10 lakh applies in some special category States for goods.
₹20 lakh is the services threshold.
₹1 crore is not the general goods threshold.
questions.tip: Goods 40, services 20. Remember it as goods being heavier, so the number is bigger.
questions.improve: List the special category States and their lower thresholds.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.history: NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission, which was also non-constitutional.
questions.discussion: Constitutional bodies derive existence from the Constitution itself, so abolishing them needs an amendment. Statutory bodies need a law, and executive bodies need only a cabinet decision.

wh.what: A policy think tank of the Government of India
wh.who: Created by Cabinet resolution, chaired by the Prime Minister
wh.why: To shift from central planning to cooperative federalism

questions.status: Active; publishes the SDG India Index and Multidimensional Poverty Index, and drives Aspirational Districts.
why_wrong: UPSC is under Article 315.
Finance Commission is under Article 280.
Election Commission is under Article 324.
questions.tip: Sort bodies into three buckets: constitutional (UPSC, EC, FC, CAG, Attorney General), statutory (NHRC, SEBI, RBI), executive (NITI Aayog, Zonal Councils).
questions.improve: Make a 20-row chart of bodies with their source article or Act; this alone covers many prelims questions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rocket moving forward by expelling gases backward is an application of:
questions.history: Newton's third law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction, and rocket propulsion is the standard illustration of momentum conservation.
questions.discussion: The rocket does not push against air, which is why it works in vacuum. The expelled mass carries momentum backward and the rocket gains equal momentum forward.

wh.how: Momentum conservation in an isolated system
wh.why: It explains motion without an external medium

questions.status: The same principle governs jet engines, ion thrusters and the recoil of a gun.
why_wrong: The first law explains inertia, not propulsion.
The second law gives the force from the mass flow rate, but the origin is the third law.
Gravitation is the force that acts on the rocket, not the propulsion mechanism.
questions.tip: For every action-reaction question, identify the two bodies exchanging force. If there are two, it is the third law.
questions.improve: Compute the thrust of a rocket expelling 5 kg per second at 2,000 m/s.
questions.source: NCERT Class XI Physics, Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Accountancy
questions.q: Which of the following is a nominal account?
questions.history: Accounts are classified as personal, real and nominal; nominal accounts cover expenses, losses, incomes and gains, and are closed to the profit and loss account.
questions.discussion: Wages is an expense, so it is nominal. Cash and bank are real accounts, and debtors is a personal account, which is why the classification decides the rule applied.

wh.how: Personal: persons and firms. Real: assets. Nominal: expenses and incomes
wh.why: The classification decides the debit-credit rule

questions.status: Computerised accounting preserves the same classification in the chart of accounts.
why_wrong: Cash is a real account, an asset in hand.
Debtors is a personal account representing people who owe money.
Bank is a real account, an asset at the bank.
questions.tip: Nominal equals name of an expense or income. If you can call it a cost or a earning, it is nominal.
questions.improve: Classify twenty common accounts into personal, real and nominal without looking them up.
